        get_wrist_cam_frames.pipeline = getattr(get_wrist_cam_frames, 'pipeline', None)
    
        if get_wrist_cam_frames.pipeline is None:
            get_wrist_cam_frames.pipeline = start_d405(exposure='auto')[0]
    
        frames = get_wrist_cam_frames.pipeline.wait_for_frames()
        depth_frame = frames.get_depth_frame()
        color_frame = frames.get_color_frame()
        depth_image = np.asanyarray(depth_frame.get_data())
        color_image = np.asanyarray(color_frame.get_data())
        last_wrist_frames = (color_image, depth_image, time.time())
        return color_image, depth_image
    
    def get_head_depth_frame():
        """Get depth frame from head camera, using cache if fresh."""
        global last_head_frames
        current_time = time.time()
    
        # Check if cached frame is fresh (< 1/60 second old)
        if last_head_frames[2] > 0 and (current_time - last_head_frames[2]) < 1/60:
            return last_head_frames[1]  # Return cached depth
    
        # Cache is stale, get fresh frames
        _, depth = get_head_cam_frames()
        return depth
    
    def get_head_rgb_frame():
        """Get RGB frame from head camera, using cache if fresh."""
        global last_head_frames
        current_time = time.time()
    
        # Check if cached frame is fresh (< 1/60 second old)
        if last_head_frames[2] > 0 and (current_time - last_head_frames[2]) < 1/60:
            return last_head_frames[0]  # Return cached RGB
    
        # Cache is stale, get fresh frames
        rgb, _ = get_head_cam_frames()
        return rgb
    
    def get_wrist_depth_frame():
        """Get depth frame from wrist camera, using cache if fresh."""
        global last_wrist_frames
        current_time = time.time()
    
        # Check if cached frame is fresh (< 1/60 second old)
        if last_wrist_frames[2] > 0 and (current_time - last_wrist_frames[2]) < 1/60:
            return last_wrist_frames[1]  # Return cached depth
    
        # Cache is stale, get fresh frames
        _, depth = get_wrist_cam_frames()
        return depth
    
    def get_wrist_rgb_frame():
        """Get RGB frame from wrist camera, using cache if fresh."""
        global last_wrist_frames
        current_time = time.time()
    
        # Check if cached frame is fresh (< 1/60 second old)
        if last_wrist_frames[2] > 0 and (current_time - last_wrist_frames[2]) < 1/60:
            return last_wrist_frames[0]  # Return cached RGB
    
        # Cache is stale, get fresh frames
        rgb, _ = get_wrist_cam_frames()
        return rgb
    
    def get_wide_cam_frames():
        get_wide_cam_frames.cap = getattr(get_wide_cam_frames, 'cap', None)
    
        if get_wide_cam_frames.cap is None:
            cap = cv2.VideoCapture(6)
            if not cap.isOpened():
                raise RuntimeError("Failed to open wide-angle camera at /dev/video6")
            cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_BUFFERSIZE, 1)
            get_wide_cam_frames.cap = cap
    
        ret, frame = get_wide_cam_frames.cap.read()
        if ret:
            return cv2.rotate(frame, cv2.ROTATE_90_COUNTERCLOCKWISE)
        return None
    
    def stop_head_cam():
        """Stop and cleanup head camera pipeline"""
        if hasattr(get_head_cam_frames, 'pipeline') and get_head_cam_frames.pipeline:
            get_head_cam_frames.pipeline.stop()
            get_head_cam_frames.pipeline = None
    
    def stop_wrist_cam():
        """Stop and cleanup wrist camera pipeline"""
        if hasattr(get_wrist_cam_frames, 'pipeline') and get_wrist_cam_frames.pipeline:
    
            # Setup object finder (shared across cameras)
            finder = MultiFinder([
                ArucubeFinder(ArucoFinder(dictionary=cv2.aruco.DICT_4X4_50, ids=[0, 1, 2])),
                YoloFinder(weights="tennis.pt", conf=0.4),
            ])
    
            # Initialize two-camera tracker
            tracker = MultiCamTracker(
                object_finder=finder,
                primary_cam_info=HEAD_CAMERA,
                secondary_cam_info=WRIST_CAMERA,
                robot_transforms=robot_transforms,
                position_threshold=0.2,
                fusion_threshold=0.35
            )
    
            print("Multi-camera tracker initialized")
            print("Press ESC to exit")
    
            while True:
                # Get frames from both cameras
                primary_rgb, primary_depth = HEAD_CAMERA.get_frames()
                secondary_rgb, secondary_depth = WRIST_CAMERA.get_frames()
    
                # Create drawing frames
                primary_drawing = primary_rgb.copy()
                secondary_drawing = secondary_rgb.copy()
    
                # Update tracker
                tracker.update(
                    (primary_rgb, primary_depth, primary_drawing),
                    (secondary_rgb, secondary_depth, secondary_drawing)
                )
    
                # Display results
                print(f"Global objects: {len(tracker.global_objects)}")
    
                # Resize and display frames
                primary_display = cv2.resize(primary_drawing, None, fx=2, fy=2, interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
                secondary_display = cv2.resize(secondary_drawing, None, fx=2, fy=2, interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
    
                cv2.imshow('Primary Camera (Head)', primary_display)
                cv2.imshow('Secondary Camera (Wrist)', secondary_display)
    
                # Allow user control
                cmd = hc.hybridize({})  # Human override
                controller.set_command(cmd)

                key = cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF
                if key == 27:  # ESC key
                    break
    
        finally:
            cv2.destroyAllWindows()
            stop_all_cameras()
            robot.stop()

## Assistant

I’ve traced the persistence pipeline, including the detector identities, 3D localization, motion compensation, and two-camera tracking. No files were changed or robot code executed.

The central idea is: **remember an object’s position in world coordinates, then associate new detections with it using identity and 3D proximity.** It is not pixel-based tracking.

### 1. Detections become world-space observations

[object_finder.py](<C:/Users/SAMMY_LOQ/Desktop/SilentSammy stretch_workspace dev sam/object_finder.py:7>) produces objects containing an image polygon, centroid, detection timestamp, and identifying attributes.

“Identical” means indistinguishable by the detector—not necessarily the same physical object:

- YOLO objects compare by `class_id`; confidence and bounding-box position are ignored.
- ArUco objects compare marker ID and dictionary.
- Arucubes compare cube ID and dictionary, ignoring the number of visible faces.

[object_locator.py](<C:/Users/SAMMY_LOQ/Desktop/SilentSammy stretch_workspace dev sam/object_locator.py:195>) samples depth near the detected centroid, back-projects it into camera coordinates, and transforms it through:

`camera → robot base → world`

Camera-to-base transforms come from robot joint positions and URDF kinematics. Base-to-world comes from odometry.

The remembered geometry is principally a **3D point**, not the object’s full shape or bounding volume.

### 2. New observations are associated with existing tracks

[object_persistor.py](<C:/Users/SAMMY_LOQ/Desktop/SilentSammy stretch_workspace dev sam/object_persistor.py:59>) first groups observations and tracks by identity.

Within each compatible group, it builds a matrix of Euclidean distances between their **world-space positions**. Hungarian assignment selects one-to-one associations, and only pairs closer than the position threshold are accepted—**20 cm by default**.

This lets several objects of the same class receive separate persistent IDs.

A successful match preserves the persistent ID but replaces its stored observation with the latest one. There is no position averaging, velocity estimate, or accumulated observation history.

### 3. Tracks have an admission and expiry lifecycle

Each `PersistentObject` stores its ID, latest observation, visibility, timestamps, and probation status.

| Event | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Unmatched new detection | Create a new persistent ID |
| Repeated matches | Progress through probation |
| Missing during probation | Fail probation and remove the track |
| Missing after approval | Keep its last world-space position, mark it unseen |
| Reliability falls below threshold | Remove the track |

Default probation is **one second**. Passing requires being matched at every processed update during that period.

An unseen approved track’s reliability decays exponentially, with a **five-second half-life**. With the default removal threshold of `0.5`, it survives approximately five seconds without another match.

That “reliability” is a freshness measure—not detector confidence.

### 4. Remembered objects are reprojected as the robot moves

[LocatedObject.account_for_motion()](<C:/Users/SAMMY_LOQ/Desktop/SilentSammy stretch_workspace dev sam/object_locator.py:49>) holds the last observed world position fixed, then transforms it into the **current** robot-base and camera frames.

Consequently, an object can remain marked—and usable by visual servoing—even when no longer detected.

This compensates for **camera/robot motion**, but assumes an unseen object remains stationary. It does not predict independent object movement.

### 5. Two-camera persistence sits above this

[multicam_tracker.py](<C:/Users/SAMMY_LOQ/Desktop/SilentSammy stretch_workspace dev sam/multicam_tracker.py:90>) runs one persistor per camera, then matches approved tracks across cameras using the same identity-and-world-distance approach.

Matched camera tracks share a global ID. If only one camera has a track, its remembered position can be projected into the other camera.

This links observations; it does not statistically fuse their positions.

### What carries over to our current project

The architecture maps well onto what we have:

- Tabletop segmentation supplies object observations and 3D geometry.
- Board-based camera localization supplies a fixed reference frame instead of robot odometry.
- Dictionary/OCR results supply additional identity evidence.

Two adaptations matter: **uncertain OCR should not automatically break an existing association**, and persistence must use **recording timestamps**, not wall-clock time. Backward frame navigation would also need replay/reset or saved tracking states.

So the reusable core is identity-aware 3D association, stable IDs, admission/expiry rules, and reprojection—not the robot-specific camera or motion-control modules.

    """RGB-D viewer with hover inspection. Focus either window and press n, p, or q."""
    
    import cv2
    import numpy as np
    from time import perf_counter
    
    from rgbd_projection import Projector
    
    
    def _resize(image, max_dimension):
        height, width = image.shape[:2]
        if max_dimension is None:
            return image
        scale = max_dimension / max(height, width)
        size = (max(1, round(width * scale)), max(1, round(height * scale)))
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_AREA if scale < 1 else cv2.INTER_LINEAR
        return cv2.resize(image, size, interpolation=interpolation)
    
    
    def _native_pixel(x, y, display_shape, native_shape):
        """Map the center of a display pixel to the corresponding source pixel."""
        dh, dw = display_shape[:2]
        nh, nw = native_shape[:2]
        return min(nw - 1, int((x + 0.5) * nw / dw)), min(nh - 1, int((y + 0.5) * nh / dh))
    
    
    def _display_pixel(u, v, display_shape, native_shape):
        dh, dw = display_shape[:2]
        nh, nw = native_shape[:2]
        x, y = round((u + 0.5) * dw / nw - 0.5), round((v + 0.5) * dh / nh - 0.5)
        return int(np.clip(x, 0, dw - 1)), int(np.clip(y, 0, dh - 1))
    
    
    def _depth_pixel(inverse, u, v, radius=3):
        """Nearest measured inverse-map entry within radius RGB pixels, or None."""
        h,w = inverse.shape[:2]
        x0,y0 = max(0,u-radius),max(0,v-radius)
        patch = inverse[y0:min(h,v+radius+1),x0:min(w,u+radius+1)]
        ys,xs = np.nonzero(patch[:,:,0] >= 0)
        distance = (xs+x0-u)**2 + (ys+y0-v)**2
        within = distance <= radius**2
        if not np.any(within):
            return None
        nearest = np.argmin(np.where(within,distance,np.inf))
        return patch[ys[nearest],xs[nearest]], distance[nearest] != 0
    
    
    def view(source, *, max_dimension=None, depth_range=(0.25, 2.0)):
        """Browse source[index] frames with RGB uint8 color and depth in meters.
    
        n: next, p: previous, q: quit. Closing either window also exits.
        Hover marks only the other window. RGB lookup uses the nearest measured
        sample within 3 RGB pixels; approximate matches are labeled in the terminal.
        Native pixel coordinates/depth in meters are printed in the terminal.
        source.calibration supplies color/depth Cameras and a depth_to_color matrix.
        Display resizing and colorization do not modify the source arrays.
        max_dimension sets each image's longer axis in pixels, including upscaling.
        Leave it as None to display at native resolution.
        """
        count = len(source)
        if not count:
            print("No frames to display.")
            return
        near, far = depth_range
        if max_dimension is not None and (not isinstance(max_dimension, int) or max_dimension <= 0):
            raise ValueError("max_dimension must be a positive integer or None")
        if not np.isfinite([near, far]).all() or far <= near:
            raise ValueError("Require finite near < far")
    
        windows = ("RGB", "Depth")
        index, displayed = 0, None
        panes = {}
        mapping = None
        inverse = None
        projector = None
        calibration = source.calibration
    
        def on_mouse(event, x, y, flags, name):
            if event != cv2.EVENT_MOUSEMOVE or name not in panes:
                return
            image, native = panes[name]
            height, width = image.shape[:2]
            if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
                return
            u, v = _native_pixel(x, y, image.shape, native.shape)
            # Clear the previous match; the hovered window uses its native cursor.
            target = "RGB" if name == "Depth" else "Depth"
            target_image, target_native = panes[target]
            overlay = target_image.copy()
            corresponding = None
            text = f"Frame {index} | {name} pixel ({u}, {v})"
            if name == "Depth":
                meters = float(native[v, u])
                text += f" | {meters:.3f} m" if np.isfinite(meters) and meters > 0 else " | invalid depth"
                if np.isfinite(mapping[v,u]).all():
                    corresponding = mapping[v,u]
            else:
                match = _depth_pixel(inverse,u,v)
                if match is not None:
                    corresponding, approximate = match
                    du,dv = corresponding
                    text += f" | depth ({du}, {dv}): {target_native[dv,du]:.3f} m"
                    if approximate:
                        text += " | nearby sample"
            if corresponding is not None:
                point = _display_pixel(*corresponding,target_image.shape,target_native.shape)
                cv2.drawMarker(overlay,point,(255,0,255),cv2.MARKER_CROSS,15,1)
            else:
                text += f" | no {target} match"
            cv2.imshow(name,image)  # Remove any marker from the hovered window.
            cv2.imshow(target,overlay)
            print(f"\r{text:<100}", end="", flush=True)
    
        try:
            for name in windows:
                cv2.namedWindow(name, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
                cv2.setMouseCallback(name, on_mouse, name)
            while True:
                if index != displayed:
                    frame = source[index]
                    if projector is None or projector.depth_shape != frame.depth.shape or projector.color_shape != frame.color.shape[:2]:
                        projector = Projector(

                            depth_D=calibration.depth.D,color_D=calibration.color.D,
                            depth_model=calibration.depth.distortion_model,
                            color_model=calibration.color.distortion_model,
                        )
                    started = perf_counter()
                    mapping,inverse = projector.build_maps(frame.depth)
                    map_ms = (perf_counter() - started) * 1000
                    color = _resize(cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR), max_dimension)
                    valid = np.isfinite(frame.depth) & (frame.depth > 0)
                    values = np.where(valid, frame.depth, near)
                    values = np.clip((values - near) / (far - near) * 255, 0, 255)
                    depth = cv2.applyColorMap(values.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLORMAP_TURBO)
                    depth[~valid] = 0
                    depth = _resize(depth, max_dimension)
                    panes = {"RGB": (color, frame.color), "Depth": (depth, frame.depth)}
                    cv2.imshow(windows[0], color)
                    cv2.imshow(windows[1], depth)
                    print(f"\r{f'Frame {index} | map {map_ms:.1f} ms | hover to inspect':<100}", end="", flush=True)
                    if displayed is None:
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[0], 20, 40)
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[1], 40 + color.shape[1], 40)
                    displayed = index
    
                key = cv2.waitKey(20)
                try:
                    if any(cv2.getWindowProperty(name, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1 for name in windows):
                        break
                except cv2.error:
                    break  # A closed window may already have been removed by its backend.
                if key < 0:
                    continue
                key = chr(key & 0xFF).lower()
                if key == "q":
                    break
                if key == "n":
                    index = min(index + 1, count - 1)
                elif key == "p":
                    index = max(index - 1, 0)
        finally:
            print()
            for name in windows:
                try:
                    cv2.destroyWindow(name)
                except cv2.error:
                    pass  # The user may already have closed this window.

    from board_est import BoardPlotter3D, get_cam_T
    from board_pose_setup import (
        DEFAULT_BOARD_SCALE, DEFAULT_DICTIONARY, DEFAULT_ROTATIONS, letter_board, make_estimator,
    )
    from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
    
    
    def _resize(image, max_dimension):
        """Match the RGB-D viewer's display sizing, including upscaling."""
        if max_dimension is None:
            return image
        height, width = image.shape[:2]
        scale = max_dimension / max(height, width)
        size = (max(1, round(width * scale)), max(1, round(height * scale)))
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_AREA if scale < 1 else cv2.INTER_LINEAR
        return cv2.resize(image, size, interpolation=interpolation)
    
    
    def estimate_frame(source, index, estimator):
        """Return an annotated BGR image and the existing estimator's result."""
        frame = source[index]
        image = cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR)
        result = estimator.get_board_transform(image)
        lines = [f"Frame {index}/{len(source) - 1} | n next | p previous | q quit"]
        if result is None:
            lines.append("No board pose (requires at least 2 board markers)")
        else:
            board_to_camera, pnp = result
            camera_to_board = get_cam_T(board_to_camera)
            position = camera_to_board[:3, 3]
            object_points = np.column_stack((pnp.obj_pts, np.zeros(len(pnp.obj_pts))))
            projected, _ = cv2.projectPoints(
                object_points, pnp.rvec, pnp.tvec, estimator.K, estimator.D
            )
            residuals = projected.reshape(-1, 2) - pnp.img_pts
            rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(np.sum(residuals ** 2, axis=1)))
            pnp.draw_axes(image, estimator.K, estimator.D, 0.05)
            for point in pnp.original_img_pts:
                cv2.circle(image, tuple(np.rint(point).astype(int)), 3, (0, 255, 0), 1)
            lines.extend([
                f"Board markers: {len(pnp.img_pts) // 4}/{len(estimator.config.board_marker_ids)} "
                f"| reprojection RMS: {rms:.2f} px",
                f"RGB camera XYZ in board (m): {position[0]:+.3f}, "
                f"{position[1]:+.3f}, {position[2]:+.3f}",
            ])
        for row, text in enumerate(lines):
            origin = (10, 25 + row * 25)
            cv2.putText(image, text, origin, cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5,
                        (0, 0, 0), 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
            cv2.putText(image, text, origin, cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5,
                        (255, 255, 255), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
        return image, result
    
    
    def browse(bag, *, rotations=DEFAULT_ROTATIONS, start_frame=0, axis_limit=1.5,
               dictionary=None, board_scale=None, max_dimension=None):
        if max_dimension is not None and (
            not isinstance(max_dimension, int) or max_dimension <= 0
        ):
            raise ValueError("max_dimension must be a positive integer or None")
        with RealSenseReader(bag, rotations=rotations) as source:
            if not 0 <= start_frame < len(source):
                raise ValueError(f"start frame must be between 0 and {len(source) - 1}")
            board = None
            if dictionary is not None or board_scale is not None:
                board = letter_board(
                    dictionary if dictionary is not None else DEFAULT_DICTIONARY,
                    board_scale if board_scale is not None else DEFAULT_BOARD_SCALE,
                )
            estimator = make_estimator(source.calibration.color, board)
            board = estimator.config
            plotter = BoardPlotter3D(
                board, axis_limit=axis_limit, update_interval=1, camera_at_origin=False
            )
            window = "RGB camera / letter GridBoard"
            try:
                # Show both sides of the board plane using the existing board axes.
                plotter.ax.set_zlim(-axis_limit, axis_limit)
                plotter.ax.set_box_aspect((1, 1, 1))
                cv2.namedWindow(window, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
                print(f"Loaded {len(source)} frames; clockwise quarter-turns: {rotations}")
                print("Board marker size: "
                      f"{board.marker_length * 1000:.2f} mm; content width: "
                      f"{board.board_width * 1000:.2f} mm")
                print("Focus RGB window: n next, p previous, q quit. RGB axes: X right, Y down, Z forward.")
                index = start_frame
                dirty = True
                while plotter.plt.fignum_exists(plotter.fig.number):
                    if dirty:
                        image, result = estimate_frame(source, index, estimator)
                        if result is not None:
                            # Pass board-to-camera unchanged: the existing plotter
                            # performs the inversion when camera_at_origin=False.
                            plotter.update(result[0])
                        else:
                            for artist in plotter.board_quivers:
                                artist.remove()
                            plotter.board_quivers.clear()
                        status = "pose available" if result is not None else "no pose"
                        plotter.ax.set_title(f"RGB camera in board frame | frame {index} | {status}")
                        plotter.fig.canvas.draw_idle()
                        cv2.imshow(window, _resize(image, max_dimension))
                        dirty = False
                    plotter.fig.canvas.flush_events()
                    key = cv2.waitKeyEx(20)
                    try:
                        if cv2.getWindowProperty(window, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1:
                            break
                    except cv2.error:
                        break
                    if key < 0:
                        continue
                    command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower()
                    if command == "q":
                        break
                    next_index = index
                    if command == "n":
                        next_index = min(index + 1, len(source) - 1)
                    elif command == "p":
                        next_index = max(index - 1, 0)
                    dirty = next_index != index
                    index = next_index
            finally:
                cv2.destroyAllWindows()
                plotter.close()
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("--rotations", type=int, choices=range(4), default=DEFAULT_ROTATIONS,
                            help=f"clockwise quarter-turns applied by the reader (default: {DEFAULT_ROTATIONS})")
        parser.add_argument("--start-frame", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--dictionary", choices=("4x4", "5x5"),
                            help="override the configured BOARD with a letter board of this dictionary")
        parser.add_argument("--axis-limit", type=float, default=1.5,
                            help="3D plot extent in each direction, meters (default: 1.5)")
        parser.add_argument("--board-scale", type=float,
                            help=f"override letter board print scale (configured: {DEFAULT_BOARD_SCALE})")
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int,
                            help="set RGB image's longer axis in pixels (default: native size)")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        if not args.bag.is_file():
            parser.error("bag must be an existing recording")
        if not np.isfinite(args.axis_limit) or args.axis_limit <= 0:
            parser.error("axis-limit must be finite and positive")
        if args.board_scale is not None and (not np.isfinite(args.board_scale) or args.board_scale <= 0):
            parser.error("board-scale must be finite and positive")
        if args.max_dimension is not None and args.max_dimension <= 0:
            parser.error("max-dimension must be positive")
        browse(args.bag, rotations=args.rotations, start_frame=args.start_frame,
               axis_limit=args.axis_limit, dictionary=args.dictionary,
               board_scale=args.board_scale, max_dimension=args.max_dimension)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()
    """Remember clicked RGB-D points in the board frame and predict their RGB pixels.
    
    Points are assumed stationary relative to BOARD in board_pose_setup.py.
    Only the board is detected on later frames; object appearance is never tracked.
    Click either image to add a point. n/p step, f/b jump, r return to the last
    selection frame, u undo, c clear, q quit. Predictions also mark occluded points.
    """
    
    import argparse
    from time import perf_counter
    
    import cv2
    import numpy as np
    
    from board_pose_setup import DEFAULT_ROTATIONS, make_estimator
    from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
    from rgbd_db3_viewer import _resize, _native_pixel, _display_pixel, _depth_pixel
    from rgbd_projection import Projector
    
    
    def remember_point(pixel, color_z, pose, camera):
        """Original RGB pixel + measured RGB-camera Z -> public board coordinates."""
        board_to_camera, pnp = pose
        # The estimator rotates corners before PnP; its pixel mapping is self-inverse.
        pixel = pnp.to_image_points([pixel]).astype(np.float64).reshape(1, 1, 2)
        xy = cv2.undistortPoints(pixel, camera.K, camera.D).reshape(2)
        camera_point = np.array([xy[0] * color_z, xy[1] * color_z, color_z, 1])
        return (np.linalg.inv(board_to_camera) @ camera_point)[:3]
    
    
    def predict_points(points, pose, camera):
        """Board points -> original RGB pixels and RGB-camera Z, without new depth."""
        board_to_camera, pnp = pose
        camera_points = np.asarray(points) @ board_to_camera[:3, :3].T + board_to_camera[:3, 3]
        pixels, _ = cv2.projectPoints(camera_points, np.zeros(3), np.zeros(3), camera.K, camera.D)
        return pnp.to_image_points(pixels), camera_points[:, 2]
    
    
    def view(source, *, max_dimension=None, step=1, jump=10, initial_frame=0):
        if max_dimension is not None and max_dimension <= 0:
            raise ValueError("max_dimension must be positive")
        if step <= 0 or jump <= 0 or not 0 <= initial_frame < len(source):
            raise ValueError("Require positive step/jump and a valid initial frame")
        calibration = source.calibration
        camera = calibration.color
        estimator = make_estimator(camera)
        projector = Projector(
            calibration.depth.K, camera.K, calibration.depth_to_color,
            (calibration.depth.height, calibration.depth.width), (camera.height, camera.width),
            depth_D=calibration.depth.D, color_D=camera.D,
            depth_model=calibration.depth.distortion_model, color_model=camera.distortion_model,
        )
        windows = ("RGB memory", "Depth memory")
        remembered = []  # (board XYZ, source frame); preserved across navigation.
        index, displayed = initial_frame, None
        panes = {}
        frame = pose = mapping = inverse = None
        pose_ms = map_ms = 0
    
        def draw():
            color, depth = panes[windows[0]][0].copy(), panes[windows[1]][0].copy()
            visible = 0
            if pose is not None and remembered:
                pixels, zs = predict_points([p for p, _ in remembered], pose, camera)
                for number, ((u, v), z) in enumerate(zip(pixels, zs), 1):
                    if z <= 0 or not np.isfinite([u, v, z]).all():
                        continue
                    if not (0 <= u < camera.width and 0 <= v < camera.height):
                        continue  # Out-of-view predictions must not clamp to the image edge.
                    point = _display_pixel(u, v, color.shape, frame.color.shape)
                    cv2.drawMarker(color, point, (0, 255, 255), cv2.MARKER_CROSS, 17, 2)
                    cv2.putText(color, str(number), (point[0] + 9, point[1] - 5),
                                cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (0, 255, 255), 1)
                    visible += 1
            status = f"{len(pose[1].img_pts)//4} board markers" if pose else "NO BOARD POSE - predictions hidden"
            text = f"Frame {index} | {status} | remembered {len(remembered)}, in view {visible}"
            cv2.putText(color, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (0, 0, 0), 3)
            cv2.putText(color, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (255, 255, 255), 1)
            cv2.imshow(windows[0], color)
            cv2.imshow(windows[1], depth)
            return {windows[0]: color, windows[1]: depth}
    
        def on_mouse(event, x, y, flags, name):
            if event not in (cv2.EVENT_MOUSEMOVE, cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN) or name not in panes:
                return
            image, native = panes[name]
            if not (0 <= x < image.shape[1] and 0 <= y < image.shape[0]):
                return
            u, v = _native_pixel(x, y, image.shape, native.shape)
            if name == windows[1]:
                depth_pixel = (u, v)
            else:
                match = _depth_pixel(inverse, u, v)
                depth_pixel = None if match is None else tuple(match[0])
            if depth_pixel is None:
                if event == cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN:
                    print("No measured depth near that RGB pixel; point not added.")
                return
            du, dv = depth_pixel
            meters = float(frame.depth[dv, du])
            rgb_pixel = mapping[dv, du]
            if not np.isfinite(rgb_pixel).all() or not np.isfinite(meters) or meters <= 0:
                return
            if event == cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN:
                if pose is None:
                    print("Board pose unavailable; point not added.")
                    return
                # Store the actual depth sample, which may be near the RGB click.
                color_z = projector.rays[2][dv, du] * meters + projector.translation[2]
                point = remember_point(rgb_pixel, color_z, pose, camera)
                remembered.append((point, index))
                print(f"Point {len(remembered)} from frame {index}: board XYZ {point.round(4)} m")
            rendered = draw()
            target = windows[0] if name == windows[1] else windows[1]
            target_image, target_native = panes[target]
            overlay = rendered[target]
            pixel = rgb_pixel if target == windows[0] else (du, dv)
            point = _display_pixel(*pixel, target_image.shape, target_native.shape)
            cv2.drawMarker(overlay, point, (255, 0, 255), cv2.MARKER_CROSS, 15, 1)
            cv2.imshow(target, overlay)
    
        try:
            for name in windows:
                cv2.namedWindow(name, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
                cv2.setMouseCallback(name, on_mouse, name)
            print("Click either image: remember point. Yellow RGB crosses are predictions.")
            print(f"n/p: +/-{step}, f/b: +/-{jump}, r: last selection frame, u: undo, c: clear, q: quit")
            while True:
                if index != displayed:
                    frame = source[index]
                    native_color = cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR)
                    started = perf_counter()
                    pose = estimator.get_board_transform(native_color)
                    pose_ms = (perf_counter() - started) * 1000
                    started = perf_counter()
                    mapping, inverse = projector.build_maps(frame.depth)
                    map_ms = (perf_counter() - started) * 1000
                    valid = np.isfinite(frame.depth) & (frame.depth > 0)
                    values = np.clip((np.where(valid, frame.depth, 0.25) - 0.25) / 1.75 * 255, 0, 255)
                    depth = cv2.applyColorMap(values.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLORMAP_TURBO)
                    depth[~valid] = 0
                    panes = {
                        windows[0]: (_resize(native_color, max_dimension), frame.color),
                        windows[1]: (_resize(depth, max_dimension), frame.depth),
                    }
                    draw()
                    print(f"Frame {index}: pose {pose_ms:.1f} ms, map {map_ms:.1f} ms")
                    if displayed is None:
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[0], 20, 40)
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[1], 40 + panes[windows[0]][0].shape[1], 40)
                    displayed = index
                key = cv2.waitKey(20)
                try:
                    if any(cv2.getWindowProperty(name, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1 for name in windows):
                        break
                except cv2.error:
                    break
                if key < 0:
                    continue
                command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower()
                if command == "q":
                    break
                if command in ("n", "p", "f", "b"):
                    delta = {"n": step, "p": -step, "f": jump, "b": -jump}[command]
                    index = int(np.clip(index + delta, 0, len(source) - 1))
                elif command == "r" and remembered:
                    index = remembered[-1][1]
                elif command in ("u", "c"):
                    if command == "c":
                        remembered.clear()
                    elif remembered:
                        remembered.pop()
                    draw()
        finally:
            for name in windows:
                try:
                    cv2.destroyWindow(name)
                except cv2.error:
                    pass
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag")
        parser.add_argument("--rotations", type=int, choices=range(4), default=DEFAULT_ROTATIONS)
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int)
        parser.add_argument("--frame", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--step", type=int, default=1)
        parser.add_argument("--jump", type=int, default=10)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        with RealSenseReader(args.bag, rotations=args.rotations) as source:
            view(source, max_dimension=args.max_dimension, step=args.step,
                 jump=args.jump, initial_frame=args.frame)
        image[mask] = (0.5 * image[mask] + 0.5 * np.array([0, 255, 255])).astype(np.uint8)
        return image
    
    
    def view(source, *, max_dimension=None, depth_jump=0.01, seed_range=0.15,
             concave_angle=6, initial_frame=0):
        if not np.isfinite([depth_jump, seed_range]).all() or min(depth_jump, seed_range) <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Depth thresholds must be finite and positive")
        if max_dimension is not None and max_dimension <= 0:
            raise ValueError("max_dimension must be positive")
        if not 0 <= initial_frame < len(source):
            raise ValueError("Initial frame is outside the recording")
        if not 0 <= concave_angle <= 180:
            raise ValueError("concave_angle must be in [0, 180]")
        calibration = source.calibration
        projector = Projector(
            calibration.depth.K, calibration.color.K, calibration.depth_to_color,
            (calibration.depth.height, calibration.depth.width),
            (calibration.color.height, calibration.color.width),
            depth_D=calibration.depth.D, color_D=calibration.color.D,
            depth_model=calibration.depth.distortion_model, color_model=calibration.color.distortion_model,
        )
        windows = ("RGB selection", "Depth selection")
        index, displayed = initial_frame, None
        frame = inverse = seed = connections = None
        bases, panes = {}, {}
        selected = None
        show_hull = True
    
        def draw():
            rgb_mask = np.zeros(frame.color.shape[:2], dtype=bool)
            valid = inverse[:, :, 0] >= 0
            x, y = inverse[valid].T
            rgb_mask[valid] = selected[y, x]
            # Fill small projection holes for display only; depth selection stays exact.
            rgb_mask = cv2.dilate(rgb_mask.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8)) != 0
            text = f"Frame {index} | {selected.sum()} pixels | {'hull' if show_hull else 'raw'} | jump {depth_jump*1000:.1f} mm"
            for name, mask in zip(windows, (rgb_mask, selected)):
                if show_hull:
                    mask = convex_mask(mask)
                image = _resize(highlight(bases[name], mask), max_dimension)
                cv2.putText(image, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (0, 0, 0), 3)
                cv2.putText(image, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (255, 255, 255), 1)
                panes[name] = image
                cv2.imshow(name, image)
    
        def select():
            nonlocal selected
            started = perf_counter()
            selected = select_region(frame.depth, seed, depth_jump, seed_range, connections, calibration.depth)
            print(f"Frame {index}, depth pixel {seed}: {selected.sum():,} pixels selected "
                  f"in {(perf_counter()-started)*1000:.1f} ms; jump {depth_jump*1000:.1f} mm")
            draw()
    
        def on_mouse(event, x, y, flags, name):
            nonlocal seed
            if event != cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN or name not in panes:
                return
            image = panes[name]
            if not (0 <= x < image.shape[1] and 0 <= y < image.shape[0]):
                return
            u, v = _native_pixel(x, y, image.shape, bases[name].shape)
            if name == windows[0]:
                match = _depth_pixel(inverse, u, v)
                if match is None:
                    print("No measured depth near this RGB pixel; click elsewhere.")
                    return
                seed = tuple(match[0])
                if match[1]:
                    print("Using a nearby measured depth sample.")
            else:
                seed = (u, v)
            select()
    
        try:
            for name in windows:
                cv2.namedWindow(name, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
                cv2.setMouseCallback(name, on_mouse, name)
            print("Click either image. n/p: frames, c: clear, h: hull/raw, i/k: depth jump, q: quit.")
            while True:
                if index != displayed:
                    frame = source[index]
                    _, inverse = projector.build_maps(frame.depth)
                    started = perf_counter()
                    connections = surface_connections(frame.depth, calibration.depth, concave_angle)
                    print(f"Frame {index}: surface connections {(perf_counter()-started)*1000:.1f} ms")
                    seed = None
                    selected = np.zeros(frame.depth.shape, dtype=bool)
                    valid = np.isfinite(frame.depth) & (frame.depth > 0)
                    values = np.clip((np.where(valid, frame.depth, 0.25) - 0.25) / 1.75 * 255, 0, 255)
                    depth = cv2.applyColorMap(values.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLORMAP_TURBO)
                    depth[~valid] = 0
                    bases = {windows[0]: cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR), windows[1]: depth}
                    draw()
                    if displayed is None:
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[0], 20, 40)
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[1], 40 + panes[windows[0]].shape[1], 40)
                    displayed = index
                key = cv2.waitKey(20)
                try:
                    if any(cv2.getWindowProperty(name, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1 for name in windows):
                        break
                except cv2.error:
                    break
                if key < 0:
                    continue
                command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower()
                if command == "q":
                    break
                if command == "n":
                    index = min(index + 1, len(source) - 1)
                elif command == "p":
                    index = max(index - 1, 0)
                elif command == "c":
                    seed = None
                    selected[:] = False
                    draw()
                elif command == "h":
                    show_hull = not show_hull
                    draw()
                elif command in ("i", "k"):
                    depth_jump = max(0.001, round(depth_jump + (0.001 if command == "i" else -0.001), 6))
                    if seed is not None:
                        select()
                    else:
                        draw()
        finally:
            for name in windows:
                try:
                    cv2.destroyWindow(name)
                except cv2.error:
                    pass
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag")
        parser.add_argument("--rotations", type=int, choices=range(4), default=1)
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int)
        parser.add_argument("--frame", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--depth-jump", type=float, default=0.01,
                            help="maximum neighbor depth difference in meters (default: 0.01)")
        parser.add_argument("--seed-range", type=float, default=0.15,
                            help="maximum total depth difference from seed in meters (default: 0.15)")
        parser.add_argument("--concave-angle", type=float, default=6,
                            help="tolerated concavity in degrees (default: 6; 180 disables)")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        with RealSenseReader(args.bag, rotations=args.rotations) as source:
            view(source, max_dimension=args.max_dimension, depth_jump=args.depth_jump,
                 seed_range=args.seed_range, concave_angle=args.concave_angle, initial_frame=args.frame)

    name: context7-mcp
    description: This skill should be used when the user asks about libraries, frameworks, API references, or needs code examples. Activates for setup questions, code generation involving libraries, or mentions of specific frameworks like React, Vue, Next.js, Prisma, Supabase, etc.
    ---
    
    When the user asks about libraries, frameworks, or needs code examples, use Context7 to fetch current documentation instead of relying on training data.
    
    ## When to Use This Skill
    
    Activate this skill when the user:
    
    - Asks setup or configuration questions ("How do I configure Next.js middleware?")
    - Requests code involving libraries ("Write a Prisma query for...")
    - Needs API references ("What are the Supabase auth methods?")
    - Mentions specific frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte, Express, Tailwind, etc.)
    
    ## How to Fetch Documentation
    
    ### Step 1: Resolve the Library ID
    
    Call `resolve-library-id` with:
    
    - `libraryName`: The library name extracted from the user's question
    - `query`: What to look up in the library's documentation (improves relevance ranking)
    
    ### Step 2: Select the Best Match
    
    From the resolution results, choose based on:
    
    - Exact or closest name match to what the user asked for
    - Higher benchmark scores indicate better documentation quality
    - If the user mentioned a version (e.g., "React 19"), prefer version-specific IDs
    
    ### Step 3: Fetch the Documentation
    
    Call `query-docs` with:

    """RGB-D viewer with hover inspection. Focus either window and press n, p, or q."""
    
    import cv2
    import numpy as np
    from time import perf_counter
    
    from rgbd_projection import Projector
    
    
    def _resize(image, max_dimension):
        height, width = image.shape[:2]
        if max_dimension is None:
            return image
        scale = max_dimension / max(height, width)
        size = (max(1, round(width * scale)), max(1, round(height * scale)))
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_AREA if scale < 1 else cv2.INTER_LINEAR
        return cv2.resize(image, size, interpolation=interpolation)
    
    
    def _native_pixel(x, y, display_shape, native_shape):
        """Map the center of a display pixel to the corresponding source pixel."""
        dh, dw = display_shape[:2]
        nh, nw = native_shape[:2]
        return min(nw - 1, int((x + 0.5) * nw / dw)), min(nh - 1, int((y + 0.5) * nh / dh))
    
    
    def _display_pixel(u, v, display_shape, native_shape):
        dh, dw = display_shape[:2]
        nh, nw = native_shape[:2]
        x, y = round((u + 0.5) * dw / nw - 0.5), round((v + 0.5) * dh / nh - 0.5)
        return int(np.clip(x, 0, dw - 1)), int(np.clip(y, 0, dh - 1))
    
    
    def _depth_pixel(inverse, u, v, radius=3):
        """Nearest measured inverse-map entry within radius RGB pixels, or None."""
        h,w = inverse.shape[:2]
        x0,y0 = max(0,u-radius),max(0,v-radius)
        patch = inverse[y0:min(h,v+radius+1),x0:min(w,u+radius+1)]
        ys,xs = np.nonzero(patch[:,:,0] >= 0)
        distance = (xs+x0-u)**2 + (ys+y0-v)**2
        within = distance <= radius**2
        if not np.any(within):
            return None
        nearest = np.argmin(np.where(within,distance,np.inf))
        return patch[ys[nearest],xs[nearest]], distance[nearest] != 0
    
    
    def view(source, *, max_dimension=None, depth_range=(0.25, 2.0)):
        """Browse source[index] frames with RGB uint8 color and depth in meters.
    
        n: next, p: previous, q: quit. Closing either window also exits.
        Hover marks only the other window. RGB lookup uses the nearest measured
        sample within 3 RGB pixels; approximate matches are labeled in the terminal.
        Native pixel coordinates/depth in meters are printed in the terminal.
        source.calibration supplies color/depth Cameras and a depth_to_color matrix.
        Display resizing and colorization do not modify the source arrays.
        max_dimension sets each image's longer axis in pixels, including upscaling.
        Leave it as None to display at native resolution.
        """
        count = len(source)
        if not count:
            print("No frames to display.")
            return
        near, far = depth_range
        if max_dimension is not None and (not isinstance(max_dimension, int) or max_dimension <= 0):
            raise ValueError("max_dimension must be a positive integer or None")
        if not np.isfinite([near, far]).all() or far <= near:
            raise ValueError("Require finite near < far")
    
        windows = ("RGB", "Depth")
        index, displayed = 0, None
        panes = {}
        mapping = None
        inverse = None
        projector = None
        calibration = source.calibration
    
        def on_mouse(event, x, y, flags, name):
            if event != cv2.EVENT_MOUSEMOVE or name not in panes:
                return
            image, native = panes[name]
            height, width = image.shape[:2]
            if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
                return
            u, v = _native_pixel(x, y, image.shape, native.shape)
            # Clear the previous match; the hovered window uses its native cursor.
            target = "RGB" if name == "Depth" else "Depth"
            target_image, target_native = panes[target]
            overlay = target_image.copy()
            corresponding = None
            text = f"Frame {index} | {name} pixel ({u}, {v})"
            if name == "Depth":
                meters = float(native[v, u])
                text += f" | {meters:.3f} m" if np.isfinite(meters) and meters > 0 else " | invalid depth"
                if np.isfinite(mapping[v,u]).all():
                    corresponding = mapping[v,u]
            else:
                match = _depth_pixel(inverse,u,v)
                if match is not None:
                    corresponding, approximate = match
                    du,dv = corresponding
                    text += f" | depth ({du}, {dv}): {target_native[dv,du]:.3f} m"
                    if approximate:
                        text += " | nearby sample"
            if corresponding is not None:
                point = _display_pixel(*corresponding,target_image.shape,target_native.shape)
                cv2.drawMarker(overlay,point,(255,0,255),cv2.MARKER_CROSS,15,1)
            else:
                text += f" | no {target} match"
            cv2.imshow(name,image)  # Remove any marker from the hovered window.
            cv2.imshow(target,overlay)
            print(f"\r{text:<100}", end="", flush=True)
    
        try:
            for name in windows:
                cv2.namedWindow(name, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
                cv2.setMouseCallback(name, on_mouse, name)
            while True:
                if index != displayed:
                    frame = source[index]
                    if projector is None or projector.depth_shape != frame.depth.shape or projector.color_shape != frame.color.shape[:2]:
                        projector = Projector(
                            calibration.depth.K,calibration.color.K,calibration.depth_to_color,
                            frame.depth.shape,frame.color.shape[:2],
                            depth_D=calibration.depth.D,color_D=calibration.color.D,
                            depth_model=calibration.depth.distortion_model,
                            color_model=calibration.color.distortion_model,
                        )
                    started = perf_counter()
                    mapping,inverse = projector.build_maps(frame.depth)
                    map_ms = (perf_counter() - started) * 1000
                    color = _resize(cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR), max_dimension)
                    valid = np.isfinite(frame.depth) & (frame.depth > 0)
                    values = np.where(valid, frame.depth, near)
                    values = np.clip((values - near) / (far - near) * 255, 0, 255)
                    depth = cv2.applyColorMap(values.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLORMAP_TURBO)
                    depth[~valid] = 0
                    depth = _resize(depth, max_dimension)
                    panes = {"RGB": (color, frame.color), "Depth": (depth, frame.depth)}
                    cv2.imshow(windows[0], color)
                    cv2.imshow(windows[1], depth)
                    print(f"\r{f'Frame {index} | map {map_ms:.1f} ms | hover to inspect':<100}", end="", flush=True)
                    if displayed is None:
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[0], 20, 40)
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[1], 40 + color.shape[1], 40)
                    displayed = index
    
                key = cv2.waitKey(20)
                try:
                    if any(cv2.getWindowProperty(name, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1 for name in windows):
                        break
                except cv2.error:
                    break  # A closed window may already have been removed by its backend.
                if key < 0:
                    continue
                key = chr(key & 0xFF).lower()
                if key == "q":
                    break
                if key == "n":
                    index = min(index + 1, count - 1)
                elif key == "p":
                    index = max(index - 1, 0)
        finally:
            print()
            for name in windows:
                try:
                    cv2.destroyWindow(name)
                except cv2.error:
                    pass  # The user may already have closed this window.
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        import argparse
        from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
    
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag", help="path to a RealSense Viewer .db3 recording")
        parser.add_argument("--rotations", type=int, choices=range(4), default=0,
                            help="clockwise quarter-turns: 0, 1, 2, or 3 (default: 0)")
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int,
                            help="set each image's longer axis in pixels (default: native size)")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        with RealSenseReader(args.bag, rotations=args.rotations) as recording:
            view(recording, max_dimension=args.max_dimension)
    """Interactive tabletop segmentation and OCR: n next, p previous, q quit.
    
    python segmentation_ocr_demo.py --start-frame 137
    OCR runs in the background; outdated results never replace the current frame.
    """
    
    import argparse
    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
    from time import perf_counter
    
    import cv2
    
    from export_rgbd_ocr import annotate
    from ocr_benchmark_demo import object_regions
    from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
    from rgbd_db3_viewer import _resize
    from rgbd_ocr import RegionOCR
    
    
    def process_frame(ocr, frame, calibration, index, elapsed, label_matcher=None):
        started = perf_counter()
        error = ""
        try:
            regions = object_regions(frame, calibration)
        except RuntimeError as exc:
            regions, error = [], str(exc)
        readings = ocr.read_regions(frame.color, regions, rotations=(0, 3),
                                    min_confidence=0.3 if label_matcher else 0.8)
        image = annotate(frame, regions, readings, index, elapsed, error, matcher=label_matcher)
        print(f"Frame {index}: {len(regions)} regions, {(perf_counter()-started)*1000:.0f} ms", flush=True)
        return index, image
    
    
    def view(reader, *, start_frame=0, max_dimension=960, label_matcher=None):
        if not 0 <= start_frame < len(reader):
            raise ValueError(f"start-frame must be between 0 and {len(reader)-1}")
        if max_dimension <= 0:
            raise ValueError("max-dimension must be positive")
        ocr = RegionOCR("rapidocr")
        first_timestamp = reader[0].timestamp_ns
        index, displayed = start_frame, None
        cache, future = {}, None
        window = "Segmentation + OCR | n next | p previous | q quit"
        cv2.namedWindow(window, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
        print("Focus the image window: n next, p previous, q quit.")
        try:
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as worker:
                while True:
                    if index != displayed:
                        frame = reader[index]
                        elapsed = (frame.timestamp_ns-first_timestamp)/1e9
                        image = cache.get(index)
                        if image is None:
                            image = annotate(frame, [], [], index, elapsed)
                            cv2.putText(image, "Processing segmentation and OCR...", (558, 165),
                                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (0, 220, 255), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
                        cv2.imshow(window, _resize(image, max_dimension))
                        displayed = index
                    if future is not None and future.done():
                        completed, image = future.result()
                        cache[completed] = image
                        if len(cache) > 8:
                            cache.pop(next(iter(cache)))
                        if completed == index:
                            cv2.imshow(window, _resize(image, max_dimension))
                        future = None
                    if future is None and index not in cache:
                        future = worker.submit(process_frame, ocr, frame, reader.calibration, index, elapsed, label_matcher)
                    key = cv2.waitKey(20)
                    try:
                        if cv2.getWindowProperty(window, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1:
                            break
                    except cv2.error:
                        break
                    command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower() if key >= 0 else ""
                    if command == "q":
                        break
                    if command == "n":
                        index = min(index+1, len(reader)-1)
                    elif command == "p":
                        index = max(index-1, 0)
        finally:
            try:
                cv2.destroyWindow(window)
            except cv2.error:
                pass
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag", nargs="?", default="recordings/20261005_195417.db3")
        parser.add_argument("--start-frame", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int, default=960)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        with RealSenseReader(args.bag, rotations=1) as reader:
            view(reader, start_frame=args.start_frame, max_dimension=args.max_dimension)

    """Browse a recorded RGB-D feed with classical tabletop segmentation.
    
    Example::
    
        python tabletop_segmentation_demo.py recordings/20261005_195417.db3 --frame 137
    
    The original ``rgbd_db3_viewer.py`` remains independent of this experiment.
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import argparse
    from pathlib import Path
    from time import perf_counter
    
    import cv2
    import numpy as np
    
    from rgbd_db3_reader import Frame, RealSenseReader
    from rgbd_db3_viewer import _resize
    from rgbd_projection import Projector
    from rgbd_tabletop_segmentation import (
        TabletopSegmentationParameters,
        TabletopSegmentationResult,
        bounding_contour,
        segment_tabletop_objects,
    )
    
    
    OBJECT_COLORS = np.asarray(
        [
            (31, 119, 180),
            (255, 127, 14),
            (44, 160, 44),
            (214, 39, 40),
            (148, 103, 189),
            (140, 86, 75),
            (227, 119, 194),
            (188, 189, 34),
            (23, 190, 207),
            (255, 187, 120),
            (152, 223, 138),
            (255, 152, 150),
        ],
        dtype=np.uint8,
    )[:, ::-1].copy()  # RGB palette converted to OpenCV BGR.
    TABLE_COLOR = np.asarray((180, 180, 180), dtype=np.uint8)
    
    
    def _colorize_depth_labels(
        result: TabletopSegmentationResult,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        overlay = np.zeros((*result.object_labels.shape, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
        visible = result.table_mask.copy()
        overlay[result.table_mask] = TABLE_COLOR
        for obj in result.objects:
            mask = np.zeros(result.object_labels.shape, dtype=np.uint8)
            cv2.fillConvexPoly(mask, obj.contour_depth_pixels, 1)
            overlay[mask != 0] = OBJECT_COLORS[obj.label % len(OBJECT_COLORS)]
            visible |= mask != 0
        return overlay, visible
    
    
    def _project_overlay_to_color(
        result: TabletopSegmentationResult,
        inverse: np.ndarray,
        color_shape: tuple[int, int],
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        color_height, color_width = color_shape
        overlay = np.zeros((color_height, color_width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
        visible = np.zeros((color_height, color_width), dtype=bool)
    
        has_source = inverse[:, :, 0] >= 0
        x, y = inverse[has_source].T
        projected_labels = np.full(color_shape, -1, dtype=np.int32)
        projected_table = np.zeros(color_shape, dtype=bool)
        projected_labels[has_source] = result.object_labels[y, x]
        projected_table[has_source] = result.table_mask[y, x]
    
        # Build the RGB rectangle from projected measured pixels, not from invented
        # depths inside the filled depth silhouette.
        kernel = np.ones((3, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
        table_dilated = cv2.dilate(projected_table.astype(np.uint8), kernel) != 0
        overlay[table_dilated] = TABLE_COLOR
        visible |= table_dilated
        padding = round(result.bottom_padding_pixels * color_height / result.object_labels.shape[0])
        for label in np.unique(projected_labels[projected_labels >= 0]):
            mask = (projected_labels == label).astype(np.uint8)
            contour = bounding_contour(cv2.findNonZero(mask), color_shape, padding)
            cv2.fillConvexPoly(mask, contour, 1)
            overlay[mask != 0] = OBJECT_COLORS[int(label) % len(OBJECT_COLORS)]
            visible |= mask != 0
        return overlay, visible
    
    
    def _blend(image: np.ndarray, overlay: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        base = image
        if base.ndim == 2:
            base = np.repeat(base[..., None], 3, axis=2)
        if base.shape[2] == 4:
            base = base[:, :, :3]
        base = base.astype(np.uint8, copy=True)
        base[mask] = np.rint(0.55 * base[mask] + 0.45 * overlay[mask]).astype(np.uint8)
        return base
    
    
    def _print_result(index: int, result: TabletopSegmentationResult) -> None:
        a, b, c, d = result.plane_model
        timings = ", ".join(
            f"{name}={duration:.1f} ms" for name, duration in result.timings_ms.items()
        )
        print(
            f"frame {index}: {len(result.objects)} objects | "
            f"valid={result.valid_pixel_count:,}, "
            f"plane-voxels={result.downsampled_point_count:,}, "
            f"table={result.table_voxel_count:,}, "
            f"candidates={result.candidate_voxel_count:,}, "
            f"noise={result.noise_voxel_count:,}"
        )
        print(f"  plane: {a:+.4f}x {b:+.4f}y {c:+.4f}z {d:+.4f} = 0")
        print(f"  timing: {timings}")
        for obj in result.objects:
            x, y, z = obj.centroid_xyz
            ex, ey, ez = obj.extent_xyz
            print(
                f"  object {obj.label}: pixels={obj.pixel_count:,}, "
                f"voxels={obj.voxel_count:,}, center=({x:.3f}, {y:.3f}, {z:.3f}) m, "
                f"AABB=({ex:.3f}, {ey:.3f}, {ez:.3f}) m, "
                f"height={obj.max_height_above_plane:.3f} m"
            )
    
    
    def _render_result(
        frame: Frame,
        result: TabletopSegmentationResult,
        projector: Projector,
        index: int,
        max_dimension: int | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        projection_started = perf_counter()
        _, inverse = projector.build_maps(frame.depth)
        color_overlay, color_mask = _project_overlay_to_color(
            result, inverse, frame.color.shape[:2]
        )
        projection_ms = (perf_counter() - projection_started) * 1000
    
        depth_overlay, depth_mask = _colorize_depth_labels(result)
        segmented_depth = depth_overlay.copy()
        valid = np.isfinite(frame.depth) & (frame.depth > 0)
        values = np.where(valid, frame.depth, 0.25)
        values = np.clip((values - 0.25) / (2.0 - 0.25) * 255, 0, 255)
        depth = cv2.applyColorMap(values.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLORMAP_TURBO)
        depth[~valid] = 0
    
        for obj in result.objects:
            u, v = obj.centroid_depth_pixel
            cv2.putText(segmented_depth, str(obj.label), (round(u), round(v)),
                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (255, 255, 255), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
    
        images = {
            "RGB segmentation": _blend(cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR),
                                       color_overlay, color_mask),
            "Depth segmentation": _blend(depth, depth_overlay, depth_mask),
            "Object clusters": segmented_depth,
        }
        text = f"Frame {index} | {len(result.objects)} objects | n next | p previous | q quit"
        for name, image in images.items():
            image = _resize(image, max_dimension)
            cv2.putText(image, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX,
                        0.4, (0, 0, 0), 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
            cv2.putText(image, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX,
                        0.4, (255, 255, 255), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
            images[name] = image
        print(f"  projection/overlay: {projection_ms:.1f} ms")
        return images
    
    
    def run_demo(

    def _positive_float(value: str) -> float:
