    """Remember clicked RGB-D points in the board frame and predict their RGB pixels.
    
    Points are assumed stationary relative to BOARD in board_pose_setup.py.
    Only the board is detected on later frames; object appearance is never tracked.
    Click either image to add a point. n/p step, f/b jump, r return to the last
    selection frame, u undo, c clear, q quit. Predictions also mark occluded points.
    """
    
    import argparse
    from time import perf_counter
    
    import cv2
    import numpy as np
    
    from board_pose_setup import DEFAULT_ROTATIONS, make_estimator
    from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
    from rgbd_db3_viewer import _resize, _native_pixel, _display_pixel, _depth_pixel
    from rgbd_projection import Projector
    
    
    def remember_point(pixel, color_z, pose, camera):
        """Original RGB pixel + measured RGB-camera Z -> public board coordinates."""
        board_to_camera, pnp = pose
        # The estimator rotates corners before PnP; its pixel mapping is self-inverse.
        pixel = pnp.to_image_points([pixel]).astype(np.float64).reshape(1, 1, 2)
        xy = cv2.undistortPoints(pixel, camera.K, camera.D).reshape(2)
        camera_point = np.array([xy[0] * color_z, xy[1] * color_z, color_z, 1])
        return (np.linalg.inv(board_to_camera) @ camera_point)[:3]
    
    
    def predict_points(points, pose, camera):
        """Board points -> original RGB pixels and RGB-camera Z, without new depth."""
        board_to_camera, pnp = pose
        camera_points = np.asarray(points) @ board_to_camera[:3, :3].T + board_to_camera[:3, 3]
        pixels, _ = cv2.projectPoints(camera_points, np.zeros(3), np.zeros(3), camera.K, camera.D)
        return pnp.to_image_points(pixels), camera_points[:, 2]
    
    
    def view(source, *, max_dimension=None, step=1, jump=10, initial_frame=0):
        if max_dimension is not None and max_dimension <= 0:
            raise ValueError("max_dimension must be positive")
        if step <= 0 or jump <= 0 or not 0 <= initial_frame < len(source):
            raise ValueError("Require positive step/jump and a valid initial frame")
        calibration = source.calibration
        camera = calibration.color
        estimator = make_estimator(camera)
        projector = Projector(
            calibration.depth.K, camera.K, calibration.depth_to_color,
            (calibration.depth.height, calibration.depth.width), (camera.height, camera.width),
            depth_D=calibration.depth.D, color_D=camera.D,
            depth_model=calibration.depth.distortion_model, color_model=camera.distortion_model,
        )
        windows = ("RGB memory", "Depth memory")
        remembered = []  # (board XYZ, source frame); preserved across navigation.
        index, displayed = initial_frame, None
        panes = {}
        frame = pose = mapping = inverse = None
        pose_ms = map_ms = 0
    
        def draw():
            color, depth = panes[windows[0]][0].copy(), panes[windows[1]][0].copy()
            visible = 0
            if pose is not None and remembered:
                pixels, zs = predict_points([p for p, _ in remembered], pose, camera)
                for number, ((u, v), z) in enumerate(zip(pixels, zs), 1):
                    if z <= 0 or not np.isfinite([u, v, z]).all():
                        continue
                    if not (0 <= u < camera.width and 0 <= v < camera.height):
                        continue  # Out-of-view predictions must not clamp to the image edge.
                    point = _display_pixel(u, v, color.shape, frame.color.shape)
                    cv2.drawMarker(color, point, (0, 255, 255), cv2.MARKER_CROSS, 17, 2)
                    cv2.putText(color, str(number), (point[0] + 9, point[1] - 5),
                                cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (0, 255, 255), 1)
                    visible += 1
            status = f"{len(pose[1].img_pts)//4} board markers" if pose else "NO BOARD POSE - predictions hidden"
            text = f"Frame {index} | {status} | remembered {len(remembered)}, in view {visible}"
            cv2.putText(color, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (0, 0, 0), 3)
            cv2.putText(color, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (255, 255, 255), 1)
            cv2.imshow(windows[0], color)
            cv2.imshow(windows[1], depth)
            return {windows[0]: color, windows[1]: depth}
    
        def on_mouse(event, x, y, flags, name):
            if event not in (cv2.EVENT_MOUSEMOVE, cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN) or name not in panes:
                return
            image, native = panes[name]
            if not (0 <= x < image.shape[1] and 0 <= y < image.shape[0]):
                return
            u, v = _native_pixel(x, y, image.shape, native.shape)
            if name == windows[1]:
                depth_pixel = (u, v)
            else:
                match = _depth_pixel(inverse, u, v)
                depth_pixel = None if match is None else tuple(match[0])
            if depth_pixel is None:
                if event == cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN:
                    print("No measured depth near that RGB pixel; point not added.")
                return
            du, dv = depth_pixel
            meters = float(frame.depth[dv, du])
            rgb_pixel = mapping[dv, du]
            if not np.isfinite(rgb_pixel).all() or not np.isfinite(meters) or meters <= 0:
                return
            if event == cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN:
                if pose is None:
                    print("Board pose unavailable; point not added.")
                    return
                # Store the actual depth sample, which may be near the RGB click.
                color_z = projector.rays[2][dv, du] * meters + projector.translation[2]
                point = remember_point(rgb_pixel, color_z, pose, camera)
                remembered.append((point, index))
                print(f"Point {len(remembered)} from frame {index}: board XYZ {point.round(4)} m")
            rendered = draw()
            target = windows[0] if name == windows[1] else windows[1]
            target_image, target_native = panes[target]
            overlay = rendered[target]
            pixel = rgb_pixel if target == windows[0] else (du, dv)
            point = _display_pixel(*pixel, target_image.shape, target_native.shape)
            cv2.drawMarker(overlay, point, (255, 0, 255), cv2.MARKER_CROSS, 15, 1)
            cv2.imshow(target, overlay)
    
        try:
            for name in windows:
                cv2.namedWindow(name, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
                cv2.setMouseCallback(name, on_mouse, name)
            print("Click either image: remember point. Yellow RGB crosses are predictions.")
            print(f"n/p: +/-{step}, f/b: +/-{jump}, r: last selection frame, u: undo, c: clear, q: quit")
            while True:
                if index != displayed:
                    frame = source[index]
                    native_color = cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR)
                    started = perf_counter()
                    pose = estimator.get_board_transform(native_color)
                    pose_ms = (perf_counter() - started) * 1000
                    started = perf_counter()
                    mapping, inverse = projector.build_maps(frame.depth)
                    map_ms = (perf_counter() - started) * 1000
                    valid = np.isfinite(frame.depth) & (frame.depth > 0)
                    values = np.clip((np.where(valid, frame.depth, 0.25) - 0.25) / 1.75 * 255, 0, 255)
                    depth = cv2.applyColorMap(values.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLORMAP_TURBO)
                    depth[~valid] = 0
                    panes = {
                        windows[0]: (_resize(native_color, max_dimension), frame.color),
                        windows[1]: (_resize(depth, max_dimension), frame.depth),
                    }
                    draw()
                    print(f"Frame {index}: pose {pose_ms:.1f} ms, map {map_ms:.1f} ms")
                    if displayed is None:
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[0], 20, 40)
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[1], 40 + panes[windows[0]][0].shape[1], 40)
                    displayed = index
                key = cv2.waitKey(20)
                try:
                    if any(cv2.getWindowProperty(name, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1 for name in windows):
                        break
                except cv2.error:
                    break
                if key < 0:
                    continue
                command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower()
                if command == "q":
                    break
                if command in ("n", "p", "f", "b"):
                    delta = {"n": step, "p": -step, "f": jump, "b": -jump}[command]
                    index = int(np.clip(index + delta, 0, len(source) - 1))
                elif command == "r" and remembered:
                    index = remembered[-1][1]
                elif command in ("u", "c"):
                    if command == "c":
                        remembered.clear()
                    elif remembered:
                        remembered.pop()
                    draw()
        finally:
            for name in windows:
                try:
                    cv2.destroyWindow(name)
                except cv2.error:
                    pass
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag")
        parser.add_argument("--rotations", type=int, choices=range(4), default=DEFAULT_ROTATIONS)
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int)
        parser.add_argument("--frame", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--step", type=int, default=1)
        parser.add_argument("--jump", type=int, default=10)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        with RealSenseReader(args.bag, rotations=args.rotations) as source:
            view(source, max_dimension=args.max_dimension, step=args.step,
                 jump=args.jump, initial_frame=args.frame)
    """Step through a recording and visualize the RGB camera in the letter board frame.
    
    Run: python board_pose_demo.py recordings/20261005_194250.db3
    Focus the RGB window: n = next, p = previous, q = quit (no Enter).
    The board origin is its center; axes follow the existing BoardEstimator.
    """
    
    import argparse
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import cv2
    import numpy as np
    
    from board_est import BoardPlotter3D, get_cam_T
    from board_pose_setup import (
        DEFAULT_BOARD_SCALE, DEFAULT_DICTIONARY, DEFAULT_ROTATIONS, letter_board, make_estimator,
    )
    from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
    
    
    def _resize(image, max_dimension):
        """Match the RGB-D viewer's display sizing, including upscaling."""
        if max_dimension is None:
            return image
        height, width = image.shape[:2]
        scale = max_dimension / max(height, width)
        size = (max(1, round(width * scale)), max(1, round(height * scale)))
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_AREA if scale < 1 else cv2.INTER_LINEAR
        return cv2.resize(image, size, interpolation=interpolation)
    
    
    def estimate_frame(source, index, estimator):
        """Return an annotated BGR image and the existing estimator's result."""
        frame = source[index]
        image = cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR)
        result = estimator.get_board_transform(image)
        lines = [f"Frame {index}/{len(source) - 1} | n next | p previous | q quit"]
        if result is None:
            lines.append("No board pose (requires at least 2 board markers)")
        else:
            board_to_camera, pnp = result
            camera_to_board = get_cam_T(board_to_camera)
            position = camera_to_board[:3, 3]
            object_points = np.column_stack((pnp.obj_pts, np.zeros(len(pnp.obj_pts))))
            projected, _ = cv2.projectPoints(
                object_points, pnp.rvec, pnp.tvec, estimator.K, estimator.D
            )
            residuals = projected.reshape(-1, 2) - pnp.img_pts
            rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(np.sum(residuals ** 2, axis=1)))
            pnp.draw_axes(image, estimator.K, estimator.D, 0.05)
            for point in pnp.original_img_pts:
                cv2.circle(image, tuple(np.rint(point).astype(int)), 3, (0, 255, 0), 1)
            lines.extend([
                f"Board markers: {len(pnp.img_pts) // 4}/{len(estimator.config.board_marker_ids)} "
                f"| reprojection RMS: {rms:.2f} px",
                f"RGB camera XYZ in board (m): {position[0]:+.3f}, "
                f"{position[1]:+.3f}, {position[2]:+.3f}",
            ])
        for row, text in enumerate(lines):
            origin = (10, 25 + row * 25)
            cv2.putText(image, text, origin, cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5,
                        (0, 0, 0), 3, cv2.LINE_AA)
            cv2.putText(image, text, origin, cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5,
                        (255, 255, 255), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
        return image, result
    
    
    def browse(bag, *, rotations=DEFAULT_ROTATIONS, start_frame=0, axis_limit=1.5,
               dictionary=None, board_scale=None, max_dimension=None):
        if max_dimension is not None and (
            not isinstance(max_dimension, int) or max_dimension <= 0
        ):
            raise ValueError("max_dimension must be a positive integer or None")
        with RealSenseReader(bag, rotations=rotations) as source:
            if not 0 <= start_frame < len(source):
                raise ValueError(f"start frame must be between 0 and {len(source) - 1}")
            board = None
            if dictionary is not None or board_scale is not None:
                board = letter_board(
                    dictionary if dictionary is not None else DEFAULT_DICTIONARY,
                    board_scale if board_scale is not None else DEFAULT_BOARD_SCALE,
                )
            estimator = make_estimator(source.calibration.color, board)
            board = estimator.config
            plotter = BoardPlotter3D(
                board, axis_limit=axis_limit, update_interval=1, camera_at_origin=False
            )
            window = "RGB camera / letter GridBoard"
            try:
                # Show both sides of the board plane using the existing board axes.
                plotter.ax.set_zlim(-axis_limit, axis_limit)
                plotter.ax.set_box_aspect((1, 1, 1))
                cv2.namedWindow(window, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
                print(f"Loaded {len(source)} frames; clockwise quarter-turns: {rotations}")
                print("Board marker size: "
                      f"{board.marker_length * 1000:.2f} mm; content width: "
                      f"{board.board_width * 1000:.2f} mm")
                print("Focus RGB window: n next, p previous, q quit. RGB axes: X right, Y down, Z forward.")
                index = start_frame
                dirty = True
                while plotter.plt.fignum_exists(plotter.fig.number):
                    if dirty:
                        image, result = estimate_frame(source, index, estimator)
                        if result is not None:
                            # Pass board-to-camera unchanged: the existing plotter
                            # performs the inversion when camera_at_origin=False.
                            plotter.update(result[0])
                        else:
                            for artist in plotter.board_quivers:
                                artist.remove()
                            plotter.board_quivers.clear()
                        status = "pose available" if result is not None else "no pose"
                        plotter.ax.set_title(f"RGB camera in board frame | frame {index} | {status}")
                        plotter.fig.canvas.draw_idle()
                        cv2.imshow(window, _resize(image, max_dimension))
                        dirty = False
                    plotter.fig.canvas.flush_events()
                    key = cv2.waitKeyEx(20)
                    try:
                        if cv2.getWindowProperty(window, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1:
                            break
                    except cv2.error:
                        break
                    if key < 0:
                        continue
                    command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower()
                    if command == "q":
                        break
                    next_index = index
                    if command == "n":
                        next_index = min(index + 1, len(source) - 1)
                    elif command == "p":
                        next_index = max(index - 1, 0)
                    dirty = next_index != index
                    index = next_index
            finally:
                cv2.destroyAllWindows()
                plotter.close()
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("--rotations", type=int, choices=range(4), default=DEFAULT_ROTATIONS,
                            help=f"clockwise quarter-turns applied by the reader (default: {DEFAULT_ROTATIONS})")
        parser.add_argument("--start-frame", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--dictionary", choices=("4x4", "5x5"),
                            help="override the configured BOARD with a letter board of this dictionary")
        parser.add_argument("--axis-limit", type=float, default=1.5,
                            help="3D plot extent in each direction, meters (default: 1.5)")
        parser.add_argument("--board-scale", type=float,
                            help=f"override letter board print scale (configured: {DEFAULT_BOARD_SCALE})")
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int,
                            help="set RGB image's longer axis in pixels (default: native size)")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        if not args.bag.is_file():
            parser.error("bag must be an existing recording")
        if not np.isfinite(args.axis_limit) or args.axis_limit <= 0:
            parser.error("axis-limit must be finite and positive")
        if args.board_scale is not None and (not np.isfinite(args.board_scale) or args.board_scale <= 0):
            parser.error("board-scale must be finite and positive")
        if args.max_dimension is not None and args.max_dimension <= 0:
            parser.error("max-dimension must be positive")
        browse(args.bag, rotations=args.rotations, start_frame=args.start_frame,
               axis_limit=args.axis_limit, dictionary=args.dictionary,
               board_scale=args.board_scale, max_dimension=args.max_dimension)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    ### Play video from file with OpenCV
    
    Source: https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/5.x/doc/py_tutorials/py_gui/py_video_display/py_video_display.markdown
    
    Plays a video file by reading frames in a loop, converting each to grayscale, and displaying them. The loop breaks when the stream ends or the user presses 'q'. Use a waitKey delay of 25 ms for normal speed; adjust for slow motion. Requires a proper ffmpeg or gstreamer installation.
    
    ```python
    import numpy as np
    import cv2 as cv
    
    cap = cv.VideoCapture('vtest.avi')
    
    while cap.isOpened():
        ret, frame = cap.read()
    
        # if frame is read correctly ret is True
        if not ret:
            print("Can't receive frame (stream end?). Exiting ...")
            break
        gray = cv.cvtColor(frame, cv.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    
        cv.imshow('frame', gray)
        if cv.waitKey(1) == ord('q'):
            break
    
    cap.release()
    cv.destroyAllWindows()
    ```

    The canonical Python sample for reading live camera frames in a real-time loop. Each iteration calls cap.read(), displays the frame with cv.imshow(), and uses cv.waitKey(1) for a 1 ms delay (essential for live streams). Press ESC to exit.
    
    ```python
        while True:
            imgs = []
            for i, cap in enumerate(caps):
                ret, img = cap.read()
                imgs.append(img)
                cv.imshow('capture %d' % i, img)
            ch = cv.waitKey(1)
            if ch == 27:
                break
    ```

    """Click an object to highlight its connected depth region on the current frame.
    
    n/p: next/previous, c: clear, h: hull/raw, i/k: adjust depth jump, q: quit.
    Selections are replaced on each click and cleared on frame changes.
    """
    
    import argparse
    from time import perf_counter
    
    import cv2
    import numpy as np
    
    from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
    from rgbd_db3_viewer import _resize, _native_pixel, _depth_pixel
    from rgbd_projection import Projector
    
    
    def surface_normals(depth, camera):
        """Estimate local surface directions from lightly denoised metric depth."""
        z = cv2.medianBlur(np.where(np.isfinite(depth), depth, 0).astype(np.float32), 5)
        dx = cv2.Sobel(z, cv2.CV_32F, 1, 0, ksize=3) / 8
        dy = cv2.Sobel(z, cv2.CV_32F, 0, 1, ksize=3) / 8
        v, u = np.indices(depth.shape, dtype=np.float32)
        K = camera.K.astype(np.float32)
        normals = np.stack((-K[0, 0]*dx, -K[1, 1]*dy,
                            z + (u-K[0, 2])*dx + (v-K[1, 2])*dy), axis=2)
        return -normals / np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(normals, axis=2, keepdims=True), 1e-9)
    
    
    def surface_connections(depth, camera, concave_angle=6):
        """Allow flat/convex neighbors; reject concave folds using camera-facing normals.
    
        The tolerance is the difference of normal-to-connection angles, in degrees.
        Geometry is cached per frame; this is a pixel-level local-convexity heuristic.
        """
        valid = np.isfinite(depth) & (depth > 0)
        # Ignore missing samples while smoothing sensor noise over a small patch.
        z = cv2.GaussianBlur(np.where(valid, depth, 0), (0, 0), 4)
        z /= np.maximum(cv2.GaussianBlur(valid.astype(np.float32), (0, 0), 4), 1e-9)
        normals = surface_normals(z, camera)
        v, u = np.indices(depth.shape, dtype=np.float32)
        K = camera.K.astype(np.float32)
        points = np.stack(((u-K[0, 2])/K[0, 0], (v-K[1, 2])/K[1, 1], np.ones_like(u)), axis=2)
        points *= z[..., None]
    
        def connected(p1, p2, n1, n2):
            delta = p2 - p1
            delta /= np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(delta, axis=2, keepdims=True), 1e-9)
            a1 = np.arccos(np.clip(np.sum(n1*delta, axis=2), -1, 1))
            a2 = np.arccos(np.clip(np.sum(n2*delta, axis=2), -1, 1))
            return a1 - a2 >= -np.deg2rad(concave_angle)
    
        connections = []
        for axis in (1, 0):
            i = np.arange(depth.shape[axis]-1)
            # Compare patches straddling each bond, not just consecutive noisy normals.
            a, b = np.maximum(i-5, 0), np.minimum(i+6, depth.shape[axis]-1)
            connections.append(connected(np.take(points, a, axis), np.take(points, b, axis),
                                         np.take(normals, a, axis), np.take(normals, b, axis)))
        return tuple(connections)
    
    
    def merge_faces(labels, seed, points, depth, depth_jump):
        """Join nearby, nearly coplanar patches split by noisy local curvature.
    
        Whole-patch planes tolerate rippled box faces without relaxing every edge.
        This intentionally cannot distinguish adjacent coplanar, touching objects.
        """
        selected = labels == labels[seed[1], seed[0]]
    
        def plane(mask):
            cloud = points[mask]
            center = cloud.mean(axis=0)
            normal = np.linalg.svd(cloud-center, full_matrices=False)[2][-1]
            return center, normal
    
        # Tiny patches do not provide a dependable plane estimate.
        if selected.sum() < 50:
            return selected
        sizes = np.bincount(labels.ravel())
        fitted = {}
        for _ in range(3):
            center, normal = plane(selected)
            near = cv2.dilate(selected.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((31, 31), np.uint8)) != 0
            _, nearest = cv2.distanceTransformWithLabels((~selected).astype(np.uint8),
                                cv2.DIST_L2, 5, labelType=cv2.DIST_LABEL_PIXEL)
            closest = points[selected]
            coordinates = np.argwhere(selected)
            changed = False
            for label in np.unique(labels[near & ~selected]):
                if label == 0 or sizes[label] < 50:
                    continue
                patch = labels == label
                gap = points[patch] - closest[nearest[patch]-1]
                distance = np.linalg.norm(gap, axis=1)
                best = np.argmin(distance)
                if distance[best] > 0.02:
                    continue
                start = np.argwhere(patch)[best]
                end = coordinates[nearest[tuple(start)]-1]
                # A short gap must contain continuous measured depth, not background
                # or missing samples between two separate, parallel objects.
                line = np.rint(np.linspace(start, end, int(np.max(abs(end-start)))+1)).astype(int)
                values = depth[line[:, 0], line[:, 1]]
                if (not np.isfinite(values).all() or np.any(values <= 0) or
                        np.any(abs(np.diff(values)) > depth_jump)):
                    continue
                if label not in fitted:
                    fitted[label] = plane(patch)
                other, direction = fitted[label]
                offset = other-center
                if (abs(normal @ direction) >= np.cos(np.deg2rad(25)) and
                        max(abs(offset @ normal), abs(offset @ direction)) <= 0.02):
                    y, x = line[len(line)//2]
                    bridge = points[max(y-4, 0):y+5, max(x-4, 0):x+5].reshape(-1, 3)
                    bridge = bridge[np.isfinite(bridge).all(axis=1) &
                                    (abs(bridge[:, 2]-depth[y, x]) <= 0.02)]
                    if len(bridge) < 10:
                        continue
                    axis = np.linalg.svd(bridge-bridge.mean(axis=0), full_matrices=False)[2][-1]
                    if min(abs(axis @ normal), abs(axis @ direction)) < np.cos(np.deg2rad(35)):
                        continue
                    selected |= patch
                    changed = True
            if not changed:
                break
        return selected
    
    
    def select_region(depth, seed, depth_jump=0.01, seed_range=0.15, connections=None, camera=None):
        """Grow through 4-connected neighbors, stopping at depth jumps or missing data.
    
        depth_jump compares neighboring pixels, not every pixel against the seed.
        seed_range additionally limits total depth drift away from the clicked point.
        Both thresholds are in meters; gaps in measured depth are not filled.
        Connections additionally forbid crossing concave surface transitions.
        When camera is supplied, nearly coplanar fragments are reunited afterwards.
        """
        x, y = seed
        valid = np.isfinite(depth) & (depth > 0)
        if not valid[y, x]:
            return np.zeros(depth.shape, dtype=bool)
        allowed = valid & (np.abs(depth - depth[y, x]) <= seed_range)
        horizontal = allowed[:, :-1] & allowed[:, 1:] & (np.abs(np.diff(depth, axis=1)) <= depth_jump)
        vertical = allowed[:-1] & allowed[1:] & (np.abs(np.diff(depth, axis=0)) <= depth_jump)
        if connections is not None:
            horizontal &= connections[0]
            vertical &= connections[1]
        # Interleave pixels and edges so OpenCV can flood a graph with blocked bonds.
        graph = np.zeros((2*depth.shape[0]-1, 2*depth.shape[1]-1), dtype=np.uint8)
        graph[::2, ::2] = allowed
        graph[::2, 1::2] = horizontal
        graph[1::2, ::2] = vertical
        if camera is not None:
            _, labels = cv2.connectedComponentsWithAlgorithm(graph, 4, cv2.CV_32S, cv2.CCL_SAUF)
            v, u = np.indices(depth.shape, dtype=np.float32)
            K = camera.K.astype(np.float32)
            points = np.stack(((u-K[0, 2])/K[0, 0], (v-K[1, 2])/K[1, 1], np.ones_like(u)), axis=2)
            points *= depth[..., None]
            return merge_faces(labels[::2, ::2], seed, points, depth, depth_jump)
        cv2.floodFill(graph, None, (2*int(x), 2*int(y)), 2, flags=4)
        return graph[::2, ::2] == 2
    
    
    def convex_mask(mask):
        """Fill the visible silhouette; never use this display hull for region growth."""
        filled = mask.astype(np.uint8)
        points = cv2.findNonZero(filled)
        if points is not None:
            cv2.fillConvexPoly(filled, cv2.convexHull(points), 1)
        return filled != 0
    
    
    def highlight(image, mask):
        image = image.copy()
        image[mask] = (0.5 * image[mask] + 0.5 * np.array([0, 255, 255])).astype(np.uint8)
        return image
    
    
    def view(source, *, max_dimension=None, depth_jump=0.01, seed_range=0.15,
             concave_angle=6, initial_frame=0):
        if not np.isfinite([depth_jump, seed_range]).all() or min(depth_jump, seed_range) <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Depth thresholds must be finite and positive")
        if max_dimension is not None and max_dimension <= 0:
            raise ValueError("max_dimension must be positive")
        if not 0 <= initial_frame < len(source):
            raise ValueError("Initial frame is outside the recording")
        if not 0 <= concave_angle <= 180:
            raise ValueError("concave_angle must be in [0, 180]")
        calibration = source.calibration
        projector = Projector(
            calibration.depth.K, calibration.color.K, calibration.depth_to_color,
            (calibration.depth.height, calibration.depth.width),
            (calibration.color.height, calibration.color.width),
            depth_D=calibration.depth.D, color_D=calibration.color.D,
            depth_model=calibration.depth.distortion_model, color_model=calibration.color.distortion_model,
        )
        windows = ("RGB selection", "Depth selection")
        index, displayed = initial_frame, None
        frame = inverse = seed = connections = None
        bases, panes = {}, {}
        selected = None
        show_hull = True
    
        def draw():
            rgb_mask = np.zeros(frame.color.shape[:2], dtype=bool)
            valid = inverse[:, :, 0] >= 0
            x, y = inverse[valid].T
            rgb_mask[valid] = selected[y, x]
            # Fill small projection holes for display only; depth selection stays exact.
            rgb_mask = cv2.dilate(rgb_mask.astype(np.uint8), np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8)) != 0
            text = f"Frame {index} | {selected.sum()} pixels | {'hull' if show_hull else 'raw'} | jump {depth_jump*1000:.1f} mm"
            for name, mask in zip(windows, (rgb_mask, selected)):
                if show_hull:
                    mask = convex_mask(mask)
                image = _resize(highlight(bases[name], mask), max_dimension)
                cv2.putText(image, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (0, 0, 0), 3)
                cv2.putText(image, text, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.4, (255, 255, 255), 1)
                panes[name] = image
                cv2.imshow(name, image)
    
        def select():
            nonlocal selected
            started = perf_counter()
            selected = select_region(frame.depth, seed, depth_jump, seed_range, connections, calibration.depth)
            print(f"Frame {index}, depth pixel {seed}: {selected.sum():,} pixels selected "
                  f"in {(perf_counter()-started)*1000:.1f} ms; jump {depth_jump*1000:.1f} mm")
            draw()
    
        def on_mouse(event, x, y, flags, name):
            nonlocal seed
            if event != cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN or name not in panes:
                return
            image = panes[name]
            if not (0 <= x < image.shape[1] and 0 <= y < image.shape[0]):
                return
            u, v = _native_pixel(x, y, image.shape, bases[name].shape)
            if name == windows[0]:
                match = _depth_pixel(inverse, u, v)
                if match is None:
                    print("No measured depth near this RGB pixel; click elsewhere.")
                    return
                seed = tuple(match[0])
                if match[1]:
                    print("Using a nearby measured depth sample.")
            else:
                seed = (u, v)
            select()
    
        try:
            for name in windows:
                cv2.namedWindow(name, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
                cv2.setMouseCallback(name, on_mouse, name)
            print("Click either image. n/p: frames, c: clear, h: hull/raw, i/k: depth jump, q: quit.")
            while True:
                if index != displayed:
                    frame = source[index]
                    _, inverse = projector.build_maps(frame.depth)
                    started = perf_counter()
                    connections = surface_connections(frame.depth, calibration.depth, concave_angle)
                    print(f"Frame {index}: surface connections {(perf_counter()-started)*1000:.1f} ms")
                    seed = None
                    selected = np.zeros(frame.depth.shape, dtype=bool)
                    valid = np.isfinite(frame.depth) & (frame.depth > 0)
                    values = np.clip((np.where(valid, frame.depth, 0.25) - 0.25) / 1.75 * 255, 0, 255)
                    depth = cv2.applyColorMap(values.astype(np.uint8), cv2.COLORMAP_TURBO)
                    depth[~valid] = 0
                    bases = {windows[0]: cv2.cvtColor(frame.color, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR), windows[1]: depth}
                    draw()
                    if displayed is None:
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[0], 20, 40)
                        cv2.moveWindow(windows[1], 40 + panes[windows[0]].shape[1], 40)
                    displayed = index
                key = cv2.waitKey(20)
                try:
                    if any(cv2.getWindowProperty(name, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1 for name in windows):
                        break
                except cv2.error:
                    break
                if key < 0:
                    continue
                command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower()
                if command == "q":
                    break
                if command == "n":
                    index = min(index + 1, len(source) - 1)
                elif command == "p":
                    index = max(index - 1, 0)
                elif command == "c":
                    seed = None
                    selected[:] = False
                    draw()
                elif command == "h":
                    show_hull = not show_hull
                    draw()
                elif command in ("i", "k"):
                    depth_jump = max(0.001, round(depth_jump + (0.001 if command == "i" else -0.001), 6))
                    if seed is not None:
                        select()
                    else:
                        draw()
        finally:
            for name in windows:
                try:
                    cv2.destroyWindow(name)
                except cv2.error:
                    pass
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag")
        parser.add_argument("--rotations", type=int, choices=range(4), default=1)
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int)
        parser.add_argument("--frame", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--depth-jump", type=float, default=0.01,
                            help="maximum neighbor depth difference in meters (default: 0.01)")
        parser.add_argument("--seed-range", type=float, default=0.15,
                            help="maximum total depth difference from seed in meters (default: 0.15)")
        parser.add_argument("--concave-angle", type=float, default=6,
                            help="tolerated concavity in degrees (default: 6; 180 disables)")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        with RealSenseReader(args.bag, rotations=args.rotations) as source:
            view(source, max_dimension=args.max_dimension, depth_jump=args.depth_jump,
                 seed_range=args.seed_range, concave_angle=args.concave_angle, initial_frame=args.frame)

    +class Playback:
    +    """Start paused; step/restart pause, and playback stops at either end.
    +
    +    Pace at the recording's FPS, without skipping frames when processing is slow.
    +    poll() also returns unhandled keys for each demo's own commands.
    +    """
    +
    +    def __init__(self, source, start_frame=0):
    +        self.count = len(source)
    +        if not 0 <= start_frame < self.count:
    +            raise ValueError(f"start-frame must be between 0 and {self.count - 1}")
    +        self.index = self.start_frame = start_frame
    +        self.interval = 1 / (source.fps or 30)
    +        self.direction = 0
    +        self.quit = False
    +        self.next_frame = 0
    +
    +    def seek(self, index):
    +        self.index = min(max(index, 0), self.count - 1)
    +        self.direction = 0
    +
    +    def update(self, key=-1, *, now=None):
    +        now = perf_counter() if now is None else now
    +        command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower() if key >= 0 else ""
    +        if command == "\x1b":
    +            self.quit = True
    +        elif command in ("a", "d"):
    +            self.direction = -1 if command == "a" else 1
    +            self.next_frame = now + self.interval
    +        elif command == "s":
    +            self.direction = 0
    +        elif command in ("q", "e", "w"):
    +            self.seek(self.start_frame if command == "w" else
    +                      self.index + (-1 if command == "q" else 1))
    +        if not self.quit and self.direction and now >= self.next_frame:
    +            self.index = min(max(self.index + self.direction, 0), self.count - 1)
    +            self.next_frame = now + self.interval
    +            if self.index in (0, self.count - 1):
    +                self.direction = 0
    +        return command
    +

    +        return self.update(cv2.waitKey(20))
    +

    Edit the vocabulary and acceptance thresholds in ocr_label_setup.py.
    """
    
    import argparse
    
    from ocr_label_setup import LABELS, MIN_MATCH_MARGIN, MIN_MATCH_SCORE
    from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
    from rgbd_label_matching import LabelMatcher
    from segmentation_ocr_demo import view

        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("bag", nargs="?", default="recordings/20261005_195417.db3")
        parser.add_argument("--start-frame", type=int, default=0)
        parser.add_argument("--max-dimension", type=int, default=960)

    # Region OCR demo
    
    Run `python ocr_benchmark_demo.py` to compare RapidOCR and EasyOCR on the five
    tabletop object crops in `recordings/20261005_195417.db3`, frame 137.
    Results and original-resolution RGB crops are saved in `ocr_benchmark/`.
    Each crop is enlarged 2x and tested at four orientations. Model loading is
    timed separately from inference; inference timings include detection and recognition.
    
    For interactive navigation with segmentation and OCR:
    
    ```powershell
    python segmentation_ocr_demo.py --start-frame 137
    ```
    
    Press `n`/`p` to move between frames and `q` to quit. OCR runs in a background
    worker so navigation stays responsive; stale results cannot replace the current
    frame. The last eight completed frames are cached. Use `--max-dimension 800`
    to resize the complete image/panel window.
    
    For known-label matching:
    
    ```powershell
    python label_matching_demo.py --start-frame 137
    ```
    
    Edit `LABELS` in `ocr_label_setup.py` to change the vocabulary and legitimate
    aliases. The demo preserves raw OCR and adds dictionary suggestions underneath.
    It normalizes accents/case/punctuation and uses normalized Levenshtein distance.
    Defaults require a similarity of at least 0.75 and a lead of at least 0.15 over
    the next canonical label. Short fragments are ignored; weaker candidates are
    marked uncertain or unknown. Matching lowers the OCR display cutoff to 0.3 so
    uncertain raw readings can be inspected; the original viewer retains its 0.8 cutoff.
    OCR confidence and dictionary similarity are distinct scores, not probabilities.
    No product identity, strength, or dosage is inferred from a label suggestion.
    
    Run `python -m unittest test_rgbd_label_matching test_rgbd_ocr` for matcher and
    OCR-coordinate tests.
    
    For a manually selected RGB region (right/bottom coordinates are exclusive):
    
    ```powershell
    python ocr_benchmark_demo.py --engines rapidocr --roi 100 200 300 500
    ```
    
    The reusable API accepts the reader's RGB arrays:
    
    ```python
    from rgbd_ocr import RegionOCR
    
    ocr = RegionOCR("rapidocr")  # Initialize once, then reuse.
    results = ocr.read_regions(frame.color, [(100, 200, 300, 500)])
    ```
    
    Results include text, engine confidence, text polygons in original full-image
    coordinates, tested crop orientation (counterclockwise), and elapsed time.
    Rotations are returned separately, rather than silently combining conflicting readings.
    Confidence is not calibrated across engines or a guarantee of correct spelling.
    Added pixels inside the object rectangles are not proof that text belongs to that object.
    
    ## Installation
    
    RapidOCR is included in `requirements.txt`; its ONNX models ship with the package.
    EasyOCR is an optional, heavier comparison engine:
    
    ```powershell
    python -m pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
    python -m pip install scipy scikit-image python-bidi ninja pyclipper shapely PyYAML Pillow
    python -m pip install easyocr==1.7.2 --no-deps
    ```
    
    The final `--no-deps` deliberately keeps the existing **GUI-enabled**
    `opencv-python`, rather than installing EasyOCR's `opencv-python-headless`
    dependency over the viewers' OpenCV. Pip may report that missing metadata
    dependency; the existing `cv2` provides the required functionality.
    EasyOCR downloads weights into `.ocr_models/easyocr/` on its first run.
    Subsequent runs are local/offline. No images are uploaded.
    
    Run `python -m unittest test_rgbd_ocr` for crop/rotation coordinate tests.

    """Coordinate and crop tests without loading OCR models."""
    
    import unittest
    
    import numpy as np
    
    from rgbd_ocr import RegionOCR
    
    
    class RegionOCRTests(unittest.TestCase):
        def setUp(self):
            self.ocr = RegionOCR.__new__(RegionOCR)
            self.ocr.engine = "rapidocr"
            polygon = [[10, 10], [20, 10], [20, 20], [10, 20]]
            self.ocr.reader = lambda image: ([
                [polygon, "label", 0.9], [polygon, "noise", 0.1]
            ], None)
            self.image = np.zeros((100, 100, 3), np.uint8)
    
        def test_rotated_polygons_return_to_original_image(self):
            readings = self.ocr.read_regions(self.image, [(10, 20, 30, 60)])
            expected = [(14.75, 24.75), (24.25, 24.75), (24.25, 54.25), (14.75, 54.25)]
            for result, point in zip(readings, expected):
                self.assertEqual(len(result.texts), 1)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(result.texts[0].polygon[0], point)
    
        def test_region_indices_and_empty_detection(self):
            self.ocr.reader = lambda image: (None, None)
            readings = self.ocr.read_regions(self.image, [(0, 0, 10, 10), (20, 20, 40, 40)], rotations=(0,))
            self.assertEqual([r.region for r in readings], [0, 1])
            self.assertTrue(all(not r.texts for r in readings))
    
        def test_invalid_crop(self):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.ocr.read_regions(self.image, [(-1, 0, 10, 10)])
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        unittest.main()

    """Shared playback tests; no GUI windows or recordings needed."""
    
    import unittest
    from types import SimpleNamespace
    from unittest.mock import patch
    
    from rgbd_db3_viewer import Playback
    
    
    class Recording:
        fps = 10
    
        def __len__(self):
            return 6
    
    
    class PlaybackTests(unittest.TestCase):
        def setUp(self):
            self.playback = Playback(Recording(), start_frame=2)
    
        def press(self, key, now=0):
            return self.playback.update(ord(key), now=now)
    
        def test_starts_paused(self):
            self.playback.update(now=100)
            self.assertEqual((self.playback.index, self.playback.direction), (2, 0))
    
        def test_play_reverse_and_pause(self):
            self.press("D")
            self.playback.update(now=0.05)
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 2)
            self.playback.update(now=0.11)
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 3)
            self.press("A", now=1)
            self.playback.update(now=1.11)
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 2)
            self.press("S", now=2)
            self.playback.update(now=100)
            self.assertEqual((self.playback.index, self.playback.direction), (2, 0))
    
        def test_step_and_restart_pause(self):
            self.press("d")
            self.press("q", now=10)
            self.assertEqual((self.playback.index, self.playback.direction), (1, 0))
            self.press("e")
            self.press("e")
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 3)
            self.press("a")
            self.press("w", now=10)
            self.assertEqual((self.playback.index, self.playback.direction), (2, 0))
    
        def test_boundaries_stop_and_steps_clamp(self):
            self.playback.seek(4)
            self.press("d")
            self.playback.update(now=1)
            self.assertEqual((self.playback.index, self.playback.direction), (5, 0))
            self.press("e")
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 5)
            self.playback.seek(1)
            self.press("a")
            self.playback.update(now=1)
            self.assertEqual((self.playback.index, self.playback.direction), (0, 0))
            self.press("q")
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 0)
    
        def test_slow_processing_does_not_skip_frames(self):
            self.press("d")
            self.playback.update(now=100)
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 3)
            self.playback.update(now=100.01)
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 3)
    
        def test_quit_and_extra_commands(self):
            self.assertEqual(self.press("H"), "h")
            self.assertFalse(self.playback.quit)
            self.press("d")
            self.press("\x1b", now=100)
            self.assertTrue(self.playback.quit)
            self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 2)
    
        def test_poll_processes_no_key_and_returns_extra_keys(self):
            self.press("d")
            with patch("rgbd_db3_viewer.cv2.waitKey", return_value=-1) as wait, \
                    patch("rgbd_db3_viewer.perf_counter", return_value=1):
                self.assertEqual(self.playback.poll(), "")
                self.assertEqual(self.playback.index, 3)
                wait.assert_called_once_with(20)
            with patch("rgbd_db3_viewer.cv2.waitKey", return_value=ord("C")):
                self.assertEqual(self.playback.poll(), "c")
    
        def test_missing_fps_uses_default(self):
            source = Recording()
            source.fps = None
            self.assertAlmostEqual(Playback(source).interval, 1/30)
    
        def test_invalid_start_frame(self):
            for index in (-1, 6):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    Playback(Recording(), index)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        unittest.main()

    +
    +class Playback:
    +    """Start paused; step/restart pause, and playback stops at either end.
    +
    +    Pace at the recording's FPS, without skipping frames when processing is slow.
    +    poll() also returns unhandled keys for each demo's own commands.
    +    """
    +
    +    def __init__(self, source, start_frame=0):
    +        self.count = len(source)
    +        if not 0 <= start_frame < self.count:
    +            raise ValueError(f"start-frame must be between 0 and {self.count - 1}")
    +        self.index = self.start_frame = start_frame
    +        self.interval = 1 / (source.fps or 30)
    +        self.direction = 0
    +        self.quit = False
    +        self.next_frame = 0
    +
    +    def seek(self, index):
    +        self.index = min(max(index, 0), self.count - 1)
    +        self.direction = 0
    +
    +    def update(self, key=-1, *, now=None):
    +        now = perf_counter() if now is None else now
    +        command = chr(key & 0xFF).lower() if key >= 0 else ""
    +        if command == "\x1b":
    +            self.quit = True
    +        elif command in ("a", "d"):
    +            self.direction = -1 if command == "a" else 1
    +            self.next_frame = now + self.interval
    +        elif command == "s":
    +            self.direction = 0
    +        elif command in ("q", "e", "w"):
    +            self.seek(self.start_frame if command == "w" else
    +                      self.index + (-1 if command == "q" else 1))
    +        if not self.quit and self.direction and now >= self.next_frame:
    +            self.index = min(max(self.index + self.direction, 0), self.count - 1)
    +            self.next_frame = now + self.interval
    +            if self.index in (0, self.count - 1):
    +                self.direction = 0
    +        return command
    +
    +    def poll(self):
    +        return self.update(cv2.waitKey(20))
    +

        from contextlib import ExitStack, redirect_stdout
        from io import StringIO
        from pathlib import Path
        from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock

        import segmentation_ocr_demo as ocr
        import board_pose_demo as board
        from rgbd_db3_reader import RealSenseReader
        from rgbd_tabletop_segmentation import TabletopSegmentationParameters
        
        class LoggedReader:
            def __init__(self, reader):
                self.reader, self.visited = reader, []
            def __len__(self):
                return len(self.reader)
            def __getitem__(self, index):
                self.visited.append(index)
                return self.reader[index]
            def __getattr__(self, name):
                return getattr(self.reader, name)
            def __enter__(self):
                return self
            def __exit__(self, *args):
                pass
        
        bag = Path('recordings/20261005_195417.db3')
        expected = [137, 138, 137, 138, 137]
        for name in ('viewer', 'selection', 'memory', 'tabletop', 'ocr', 'board'):
            with RealSenseReader(bag, rotations=1) as source, ExitStack() as stack:
                logged = LoggedReader(source)
                for function in ('namedWindow', 'setMouseCallback', 'imshow', 'moveWindow', 'destroyWindow', 'destroyAllWindows'):
                    stack.enter_context(patch.object(cv2, function))
                stack.enter_context(patch.object(cv2, 'getWindowProperty', return_value=1))
                stack.enter_context(patch.object(cv2, 'waitKey', side_effect=[ord(c) for c in 'eqew'] + [27]))
                stack.enter_context(redirect_stdout(StringIO()))
                if name == 'viewer':
                    viewer.view(logged, start_frame=137, max_dimension=400)
                elif name == 'selection':

    def reliability_to_color(normalized_reliability):
        """Convert normalized reliability to BGR color.
    
        Args:
            normalized_reliability: Reliability value in [0, 1] range
    
        Returns:
            BGR color tuple (B, G, R) interpolated from red (low) to yellow to green (high)
        """
        # Interpolate color: red (0, 0, 255) -> yellow (0, 255, 255) -> green (0, 255, 0)
        if normalized_reliability > 0.5:
            # Upper half: yellow to green
            t = (normalized_reliability - 0.5) * 2  # 0 to 1
            color = (0, 255, int(255 * (1 - t)))
        else:
            # Lower half: red to yellow
            t = normalized_reliability * 2  # 0 to 1
            color = (0, int(255 * t), 255)
    
        return color
    
    def draw_tracked_object_marker(drawing_frame, object_id, pixel_x, pixel_y, color):
        """Draw object ID and marker with specified color.
    
        Args:
            drawing_frame: Image to draw on
            object_id: Object ID number to display
            pixel_x, pixel_y: Pixel coordinates for marker
            color: BGR color tuple
        """
        # Draw ID with specified color
        text = f"{object_id}"
        cv2.putText(drawing_frame, text, (int(pixel_x), int(pixel_y) - 10),
                   cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, color, 2)
    
        # Draw circle at centroid
        cv2.circle(drawing_frame, (int(pixel_x), int(pixel_y)), 4, color, -1)
    
    def match_objects_by_identity_and_position(
        new_objects,           # List of any object type
        old_objects,           # List of any object type
        get_identity_fn,       # Function: obj -> identity object for comparison
        get_position_fn,       # Function: obj -> np.array([x, y, z]) or None
        are_identical_fn,      # Function: (identity1, identity2) -> bool
        position_threshold     # float
    ):
        """Match new objects to old objects using identity grouping and position-based Hungarian algorithm.
    
        Returns:
            Tuple of (matched_new, matched_old, match_pairs) where:
            - matched_new: set of matched new object indices
            - matched_old: set of matched old object indices
            - match_pairs: list of (new_idx, old_idx) tuples
        """
    
        def group_by_identity(objects):
            """Group objects by identity."""
            groups = []
            used = set()
    
            for i, obj in enumerate(objects):
                if i in used:
                    continue
    
                obj_identity = get_identity_fn(obj)
                group = [(i, obj)]
                used.add(i)
    
                # Find all other objects identical to this one
                for j, other_obj in enumerate(objects):
                    if j <= i or j in used:
                        continue
    
                    other_identity = get_identity_fn(other_obj)
                    if are_identical_fn(obj_identity, other_identity):
                        group.append((j, other_obj))
                        used.add(j)
    
                groups.append(group)
    
            return groups
    
        # Group new and old objects by identity
        new_groups = group_by_identity(new_objects)
        old_groups = group_by_identity(old_objects)
    
        matched_new = set()
        matched_old = set()
        match_pairs = []
    
        # For each group of new objects, find the matching group of old objects
        for new_group in new_groups:
            if not new_group:
                continue
    
            # Get a representative object from the new group
            _, new_rep = new_group[0]
            new_rep_identity = get_identity_fn(new_rep)
    
            # Find the matching old group (if any)
            matching_old_group = None
            for old_group in old_groups:
                if not old_group:
                    continue
                _, old_rep = old_group[0]
                old_rep_identity = get_identity_fn(old_rep)
    
                if are_identical_fn(new_rep_identity, old_rep_identity):
                    matching_old_group = old_group
                    break
    
            if matching_old_group is None:
                # No matching old group, these are all new objects
                continue
    
            # Build cost matrix for this group only
            group_cost_matrix = np.zeros((len(new_group), len(matching_old_group)))
    
            for i, (new_idx, new_obj) in enumerate(new_group):
                new_pos = get_position_fn(new_obj)
                if new_pos is None:
                    group_cost_matrix[i, :] = np.inf
                    continue
    
                for j, (old_idx, old_obj) in enumerate(matching_old_group):
                    old_pos = get_position_fn(old_obj)
                    if old_pos is None:
                        group_cost_matrix[i, j] = np.inf
                        continue
                    group_cost_matrix[i, j] = np.linalg.norm(new_pos - old_pos)
    
            # Skip Hungarian algorithm if matrix is degenerate or has no valid matches
            if group_cost_matrix.size == 0:
                # Empty matrix
                print(f"DEBUG: Skipping empty cost matrix")
                continue
            if np.all(np.isinf(group_cost_matrix)):
                # All costs are infinite - no valid positions
                print(f"DEBUG: Skipping all-infinite cost matrix, shape: {group_cost_matrix.shape}")
                continue
    
            # Check if there are any feasible matches (costs below threshold)
            feasible_mask = group_cost_matrix < position_threshold
            if not np.any(feasible_mask):
                # No feasible matches in this group, skip Hungarian algorithm
                print(f"DEBUG: No feasible matches below threshold {position_threshold}, min cost: {np.min(group_cost_matrix[~np.isinf(group_cost_matrix)]) if np.any(~np.isinf(group_cost_matrix)) else 'all inf'}")
                continue
    
            # Debug: Check matrix state before Hungarian
            print(f"DEBUG: Running Hungarian on matrix shape {group_cost_matrix.shape}, finite values: {np.sum(np.isfinite(group_cost_matrix))}, min: {np.min(group_cost_matrix)}, max: {np.max(group_cost_matrix[np.isfinite(group_cost_matrix)])}")
    
            # Run Hungarian algorithm on this group
            row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(group_cost_matrix)
    
            for new_i, old_i in zip(row_ind, col_ind):
                if group_cost_matrix[new_i, old_i] < position_threshold:
                    new_idx, _ = new_group[new_i]
                    old_idx, _ = matching_old_group[old_i]
    
                    matched_new.add(new_idx)
                    matched_old.add(old_idx)
                    match_pairs.append((new_idx, old_idx))
    
        return matched_new, matched_old, match_pairs
    
    class PersistentObject:
        _next_id = 0
    
        def __init__(self, located_object, persistor, id=None):
            self.located_object = located_object
            self.persistor = persistor
            self.visible = True
            self.last_seen_timestamp = located_object.image_object.timestamp
            self.last_base2world_T = located_object.base2world_T
            self.probation = 0.0  # 0.0 = starting probation, 1.0 = passed probation, -1.0 = failed probation
            self.first_seen_timestamp = located_object.image_object.timestamp  # Track when probation started
    
            if id is None:
                self.id = PersistentObject._next_id
                PersistentObject._next_id += 1
            else:
                self.id = id
    
        def update(self, new_located_object):
            """Update with new detection (called by ObjectPersistor on match).
    
            Args:
                new_located_object: LocatedObject if matched this frame, None if not seen
            """
            if new_located_object is not None:
                self.located_object = new_located_object
                self.visible = True
                self.last_seen_timestamp = new_located_object.image_object.timestamp
                self.last_base2world_T = new_located_object.base2world_T
    
                # Update probation if still in probation period
                if 0.0 <= self.probation < 1.0:
                    time_elapsed = self.last_seen_timestamp - self.first_seen_timestamp
                    probation_progress = time_elapsed / self.persistor.probation_period
                    self.probation = min(1.0, probation_progress)
            else:
                self.visible = False
    
                # Fail probation if not seen during probation period
                if 0.0 <= self.probation < 1.0:
                    self.probation = -1.0
    
        def get_reliability(self, time_decay_halflife=5.0):
            """Compute reliability factor (0.0-1.0) based on visibility and time.
    
            Args:
                time_decay_halflife: Half-life in seconds for time-based decay when not visible
    
            Returns:
                Reliability factor between 0.0 (unreliable) and 1.0 (fully reliable)
            """
            if self.visible:
                return 1.0
    
            # Time-based exponential decay when not visible
            time_elapsed = time.time() - self.last_seen_timestamp
            time_decay = np.exp(-time_elapsed * np.log(2) / time_decay_halflife)
    
            return time_decay
    
        def get_normalized_reliability(self):
            """Get reliability normalized to [0, 1] range relative to persistor's threshold."""
            reliability = self.get_reliability(self.persistor.time_decay_halflife)
            normalized = (reliability - self.persistor.reliability_threshold) / (1.0 - self.persistor.reliability_threshold)
            return np.clip(normalized, 0.0, 1.0)
    
    class ObjectPersistor:
        def __init__(self, object_locator, position_threshold=0.2, reliability_threshold=0.5, time_decay_halflife=5.0, probation_period=1.0):
            self.object_locator = object_locator
            self.tracked_objects = []
            self.position_threshold = position_threshold
            self.reliability_threshold = reliability_threshold
            self.time_decay_halflife = time_decay_halflife
            self.probation_period = probation_period
    
        def _group_by_identity(self, located_objects):
            """Group objects by identity. Objects that are identical to each other go in the same group.
    
            Returns:
                List of groups, where each group is a list of (index, located_object) tuples
            """
            groups = []
            used = set()
    
            for i, obj in enumerate(located_objects):
                if i in used:
                    continue
    
                # Start a new group with this object
                group = [(i, obj)]
                used.add(i)
    
                # Find all other objects identical to this one
                for j, other_obj in enumerate(located_objects):
                    if j <= i or j in used:
                        continue
    
                    identical = obj.image_object.is_identical_to(other_obj.image_object)
                    if identical is True:
                        group.append((j, other_obj))
                        used.add(j)
    
                groups.append(group)
    
            return groups
    
        def _match_objects_grouped(self, new_located_objects):
            """Match new detections to tracked objects by grouping identical objects first."""
            # Define accessor functions for the generic matching algorithm
            def get_identity(obj):
                # Handle both LocatedObject and PersistentObject
                if hasattr(obj, 'image_object'):
                    return obj.image_object
                else:  # PersistentObject
                    return obj.located_object.image_object
    
            def get_position(obj):
                # Handle both LocatedObject and PersistentObject
                if hasattr(obj, 'obj2world_T'):
                    return obj.obj2world_T[:3, 3] if obj.obj2world_T is not None else None
                else:  # PersistentObject
                    obj2world_T = obj.located_object.obj2world_T
                    return obj2world_T[:3, 3] if obj2world_T is not None else None
    
            def are_identical(identity1, identity2):
                return identity1.is_identical_to(identity2) is True
    
            # Use generic matching algorithm
            matched_new, matched_old, match_pairs = match_objects_by_identity_and_position(
                new_objects=new_located_objects,
                old_objects=self.tracked_objects,
                get_identity_fn=get_identity,
                get_position_fn=get_position,
                are_identical_fn=are_identical,
                position_threshold=self.position_threshold
            )
    
            # Update matched tracked objects with new detections
            for new_idx, old_idx in match_pairs:
                self.tracked_objects[old_idx].update(new_located_objects[new_idx])
    
            # Update unmatched tracked objects with None (they weren't seen this frame)
            for i, persistent_obj in enumerate(self.tracked_objects):
                if i not in matched_old:
                    persistent_obj.update(None)
    
            return matched_new, matched_old
    
        def _add_new_objects(self, new_located_objects, matched_new):
            """Create persistent objects for unmatched new detections."""
            for i, located_obj in enumerate(new_located_objects):
                if i not in matched_new:
                    persistent_obj = PersistentObject(located_obj, self)
                    self.tracked_objects.append(persistent_obj)
    
        def _remove_unreliable_objects(self):
            """Remove objects with low reliability (exponential decay for lost objects) and failed probation."""
            self.tracked_objects = [
                obj for obj in self.tracked_objects
                if obj.get_reliability(self.time_decay_halflife) >= self.reliability_threshold
                and obj.probation != -1.0  # Remove objects that failed probation
            ]
    
        def _draw_tracked_objects(self, drawing_frame):
            """Draw tracked objects with reliability-based color coding."""
            if drawing_frame is None:
                return
    
            for persistent_obj in self.tracked_objects:
                obj = persistent_obj.located_object
    
                # Get object pose accounting for robot motion
                updated_obj2base_T, updated_obj2cam_T = obj.account_for_motion()
    
                # Check if pose is valid for drawing
                if updated_obj2cam_T is None:
                    continue
    
                # Get object position on image
                pitch, yaw, distance = ObjectLocator.pose_to_polar(updated_obj2cam_T)
                pixel_x, pixel_y = self.object_locator.depth_cam_info.object_angles_to_pixel(yaw, pitch)
    
                if persistent_obj.probation >= 1.0:
                    # Draw approved objects with reliability-based color coding
                    normalized_reliability = persistent_obj.get_normalized_reliability()
                    color = reliability_to_color(normalized_reliability)
                    draw_tracked_object_marker(drawing_frame, persistent_obj.id, pixel_x, pixel_y, color)
                else:
                    # Draw unapproved objects (still in probation) with yellow question mark
                    color = (0, 255, 255)  # Yellow in BGR
    
                    # Draw question mark
                    text = "?"
                    cv2.putText(drawing_frame, text, (int(pixel_x), int(pixel_y) - 10),
                               cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, color, 2)
    
                    # Draw small circle at centroid
                    cv2.circle(drawing_frame, (int(pixel_x), int(pixel_y)), 4, color, -1)
    
        def update(self, rgb_frame, depth_frame, drawing_frame=None):
            """Detect, locate, and track objects using optimal bipartite matching."""
            # Get current camera transform and detect objects
            cam_T = self.object_locator.robot_transforms.get_cam_T( self.object_locator.depth_cam_info )
            new_located_objects = self.object_locator.locate_all(rgb_frame, depth_frame, cam_T, None)
    
            if not new_located_objects:
                # Update all tracked objects with None (no detections this frame)
                for persistent_obj in self.tracked_objects:
                    persistent_obj.update(None)
                self._remove_unreliable_objects()
                self._draw_tracked_objects(drawing_frame)
                return
    
            if not self.tracked_objects:
                # No existing objects, create new ones for all detections
                for located_obj in new_located_objects:
                    self.tracked_objects.append(PersistentObject(located_obj, self))
                return
    
            # Match new detections to existing tracked objects
            matched_new, matched_old = self._match_objects_grouped(new_located_objects)
    
            # Add new objects and remove unreliable ones
            self._add_new_objects(new_located_objects, matched_new)
            self._remove_unreliable_objects()
    
            # Draw tracked objects with reliability-based colors
            self._draw_tracked_objects(drawing_frame)
    
        def get_visible_objects(self):
            """Return list of currently visible objects that have passed probation."""
            return [obj for obj in self.tracked_objects if obj.visible and obj.probation >= 1.0]
    
        def get_approved_objects(self):
            """Return all tracked objects that have passed probation."""
            return [obj for obj in self.tracked_objects if obj.probation >= 1.0]
    
        def get_all_objects(self):
            """Return all tracked objects (including those in probation)."""
            return self.tracked_objects
    
    if __name__ == '__main__':
        try:
            # Initialize robot
            robot = rb.Robot()
            robot.startup()
            controller = nvc.NormalizedVelocityControl(robot)
    
            # Set up object persistor
            CAMERA = WRIST_CAMERA
            robot_transforms = RobotTransforms(robot)
            finder = MultiFinder([
                ArucubeFinder(ArucoFinder(dictionary=cv2.aruco.DICT_4X4_50, ids=[0, 1, 2])),
                YoloFinder(weights="tennis.pt", conf=0.4),
            ])
            locator = ObjectLocator(finder, CAMERA, robot_transforms)
            persistor = ObjectPersistor(locator, position_threshold=0.2)
    
            while True:
                # Get camera feeds
                rgb_frame, depth_frame = CAMERA.get_frames()
                drawing_frame = rgb_frame.copy()
    
                # Update persistent object tracking (includes drawing)
                persistor.update(rgb_frame, depth_frame, drawing_frame)
    
                # Debug info about tracking status
                total_tracked = len(persistor.get_all_objects())
                established = len(persistor.get_approved_objects())
                in_probation = len([obj for obj in persistor.tracked_objects if 0.0 <= obj.probation < 1.0])
                print(f"Tracking: {established} established, {in_probation} in probation ({total_tracked} total)")
    
                # Display feeds
                display_frame = cv2.resize(drawing_frame, None, fx=2, fy=2, interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
                cv2.imshow('Color Camera', display_frame)
    
                # Track object with lowest ID (only approved objects)
                approved_objects = persistor.get_approved_objects()
                if approved_objects:
                    target_obj = min(approved_objects, key=lambda obj: obj.id)
                    head_cmd = look_at_object(target_obj.located_object, CAMERA)
                else:
                    head_cmd = {}
    
                # Allow control
                cmd = hc.hybridize(head_cmd) # Human override
                controller.set_command(cmd)
    
                # Exit on ESC key or if plot window is closed
